'''Algernon Darius Crumpler''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|æ|l|dʒ|iː}}; born December 23, 1977) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for ten seasons. He was selected by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] in the second round of the [[2001 NFL draft]]. Crumpler also played for the [[Tennessee Titans]] and [[New England Patriots]]. He is a four-time [[Pro Bowl]] selection. He played [[college football]] for [[North Carolina Tar Heels football|North Carolina]]. 

==Early life==
Crumpler attended [[New Hanover High School]] in [[Wilmington, North Carolina]] and was a letterman in football and [[track and field]]. His brother is [[Carlester Crumpler]].  In football, he started as a tight end and as a [[linebacker]], and as a senior, he was an All-Midwest 4-A Conference selection. In track & field, he was a three-time [[discus]] state champion, and won a state championship in [[shot put]] in 1996. He graduated from high school in 1996.

==College career==
After graduating from high school, Crumpler attended the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]]. During his last three seasons with the Tar Heels, Crumpler was named to the All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] first-team. As a sophomore, Crumpler caught 24 passes for a total of 278 yards, with four of those catches being touchdowns. In his junior season, Crumpler had 20 catches for 191 yards. His senior season concluded with him amassing 23 catches for 287 yards and one touchdown and he finished second in All-American voting.

===Atlanta Falcons===
Crumpler was selected by the Falcons in the second round (35th overall) of the [[2001 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2001 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2001/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-18 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Crumpler made the first start of his NFL career against the [[Carolina Panthers]] on September 23, 2001. He caught his first two passes for a total of 13 yards. His first touchdown was scored against the [[New Orleans Saints]], on October 21, 2001. He finished his rookie season starting 12 of 16 games and totaling 25 receptions for 330 yards and three touchdowns. In [[2002 Atlanta Falcons season|2002]], Crumpler started 9 of 16 games, recording 36 receptions for 455 yards and five touchdowns.

Crumpler earned his first [[2004 Pro Bowl|Pro Bowl]] honor in [[2003 Atlanta Falcons season|2003]], starting all 16 games for the Falcons, catching 44 passes for 552 yards, the most for a Falcons tight end since [[1980 Atlanta Falcons season|1980]]; he also had three touchdowns. Crumpler played in and started 14 games for the Falcons in [[2004 Atlanta Falcons season|2004]], who advanced to the [[NFC Championship Game]]. Crumpler finished the regular season with 48 receptions for 774 yards and six touchdowns and was elected to the [[2005 Pro Bowl|Pro Bowl]]. In [[2005 Atlanta Falcons season|2005]], Crumpler returned to start 16 games for the Falcons, setting career highs with 65 receptions for 877 yards, as well as five touchdowns. He was also named to his third-consecutive [[2006 Pro Bowl|Pro Bowl]].

In [[2006 Atlanta Falcons season|2006]], Crumpler set a career-high with eight touchdowns, while also making 56 catches for 780 yards in 16 games started. Crumpler made 10 starts in 14 games in [[2007 Atlanta Falcons season|2007]], in his first season without [[Michael Vick]] at quarterback. He finished the year with 42 receptions for 444 yards and five touchdowns. In December 2007, Crumpler was fined by the NFL for wearing black eye strips during a ''[[Monday Night Football]]'' which had the letters MV and the number 7 written on them in support of Vick, who was in prison at the time.<ref name="Falcons fined for Vick 'support'">{{cite web |date=December 19, 2007 |title=Falcons fined for Vick 'support' |url=http://www.foxsports.com.au/breaking-news/falcons-fined-for-vick-support/story-e6frf33c-1111115148964#.UOBt6n3LdRw |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121230163835/http://www.foxsports.com.au/breaking-news/falcons-fined-for-vick-support/story-e6frf33c-1111115148964%23.UOBt6n3LdRw |archive-date=December 30, 2012 |accessdate=December 19, 2007 |work=Fox Sports |publisher=[[Reuters]]}}</ref>

On February 15, 2008, Crumpler was released by the Falcons.

===Tennessee Titans===
On March 2, 2008, Crumpler signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]]. He made his debut with the team on September 7, 2008, against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]]. He started 15 games for the Titans in [[2008 Tennessee Titans season|2008]], making 24 catches for 257 yards. In the Titans' [[2008–09 NFL playoffs|Divisional Playoff]] game against the [[Baltimore Ravens]], Crumpler fumbled after a reception from [[Kerry Collins]] on the Ravens' 5-yard line, which helped the Ravens ultimately win the game over the top-seeded Titans.

On August 9, 2009, in the Titans' first preseason game, Crumpler weighed approximately 300 pounds, gaining an estimated 30 pounds during the offseason.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nfl/columns/story?id=5044893|title=Crumpler on a mission|work=ESPNBoston.com|first=Mike|last=Reiss|date=March 31, 2010|access-date=April 2, 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100404134902/http://sports.espn.go.com/boston/nfl/columns/story?id=5044893| archive-date= April 4, 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> However, Crumpler played in all 16 games for the Titans in [[2009 Tennessee Titans season|2009]], starting 14 and catching 27 passes for 222 yards and one touchdown. He was also part of a blocking unit that aided Titans running back [[Chris Johnson (running back)|Chris Johnson]] in a 2,006-yard rushing season.

===New England Patriots===
On March 24, 2010, Crumpler signed with the [[New England Patriots]]. After running back [[Kevin Faulk]], an offensive captain, was lost for the season with a knee injury in Week 2, the team named Crumpler an offensive captain prior to their Week 6 game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.patriots.com/mediacenter/index.cfm?ac=videonewsdetail&pid=45233&pcid=155|title=Bill Belichick Postgame Press Conference - 10/17/2010|work=[[New England Patriots]]|date=October 17, 2010|accessdate=October 28, 2010|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101022020457/http://www.patriots.com/mediacenter/index.cfm?ac=videonewsdetail&pid=45233&pcid=155|archivedate=October 22, 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref> The next day, head coach [[Bill Belichick]] lauded Crumpler's professionalism:
{{cquote|He's very professional. Alge's really smart. He's into football. He works hard at it. He has a great presence. He's one of those guys that just seems like he always does the right thing no matter what the situation is. Whether it's in a game, in practice, in a meeting, in a walk through, whether it's a decision on the play, whether it's the way his demeanor is at that particular time, he knows when to smile, he knows when to be serious, he knows when to [step up], when to back off, when to gear it up, when to say and do the right thing. He's constantly helping his teammates and making reminders to them or telling them what to do to help them work off of him and so forth. I guess I think the best way I can put it is it seems like he always does the right thing no matter what the situation is. On or off the field, in the locker room, meetings, practice, it just seems like he always does the right thing.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.patriots.com/mediacenter/index.cfm?ac=videonewsdetail&pid=45255&pcid=155|title=Bill Belichick Press Conference - 10/18/2010|work=[[New England Patriots]]|date=2010-10-18|accessdate=2010-10-28|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101023130225/http://www.patriots.com/mediacenter/index.cfm?ac=videonewsdetail&pid=45255&pcid=155|archivedate=2010-10-23|url-status=dead}}</ref>}}

Crumpler finished the 2010 season with six receptions for 52 yards and two touchdowns in 16 games played (10 starts).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alge Crumpler 2010 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CrumAl00/gamelog/2010/ |access-date=2025-05-13 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> On July 29, 2011, the Patriots released Crumpler.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Underhill |first=Nick |date=2011-07-29 |title=Patriots release Alge Crumpler, Ty Warren, others |url=https://www.masslive.com/patriots/2011/07/patriots_release_alge_crumpler.html |access-date=2025-07-07 |website=masslive}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Crumpler is the son of Carlester Crumpler, a running back at [[East Carolina Pirates football|East Carolina]] who was inducted into the East Carolina University Athletics Hall of Fame in 1980 and the [[North Carolina Sports Hall of Fame]] inductee in 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Carlester Crumpler, Sr. (1980) - ECU Athletics Hall of Fame |url=https://ecupirates.com/honors/ecu-athletics-hall-of-fame/carlester-crumpler-sr-/35 |access-date=2025-07-07 |website=[[East Carolina Pirates|East Carolina University Athletics]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-01-16 |title=Carlester Crumpler |url=https://ncshof.org/2023/01/carlester-crumpler/ |access-date=2025-07-07 |website=NC Sports Hall of Fame |language=en-US}}</ref> His father was drafted by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in 1974.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1974 Buffalo Bills Draftees |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/buf/1974_draft.htm |access-date=2025-07-07 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Alge is named after his father's favorite book, ''[[Flowers for Algernon]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alge Crumpler biography |url=http://www.titansonline.com/team/roster/Alge-Crumpler/e8529d2e-9015-439f-8d18-49a5c3da7f3e |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100123090238/http://www.titansonline.com/team/roster/Alge-Crumpler/e8529d2e-9015-439f-8d18-49a5c3da7f3e |archive-date=January 23, 2010 |accessdate=April 2, 2010 |work=[[Tennessee Titans]]}}</ref>

Crumpler is the younger brother of former East Carolina, [[Seattle Seahawks]], and [[Minnesota Vikings]] tight end [[Carlester Crumpler]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carree |first=Chuck |date=2006-08-09 |title=Crumpler has seen a lot of change |url=https://www.starnewsonline.com/story/news/2006/08/09/crumpler-has-seen-a-lot-of-change/30270994007/ |access-date=2025-07-04 |website=Wilmington Star-News}}</ref> He is the half brother of A'riana Crumpler, who competed in [[Throwing sports|throwing events]] for [[East Carolina Pirates track and field|ECU's track and field team]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=A'riana Crumpler - Track & Field |url=https://ecupirates.com/sports/track-and-field/roster/a-riana-crumpler/13466 |access-date=2025-07-07 |website=[[East Carolina Pirates|East Carolina University Athletics]]}}</ref> and Isaiah Crumpler, who plays football for [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights football|Rutgers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Isaiah Crumpler - Football |url=https://scarletknights.com/sports/football/roster/isaiah-crumpler/15393 |access-date=2025-07-07 |website=[[Rutgers Scarlet Knights|Rutgers University Athletics]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Hunt |first=Todderick |date=2023-05-10 |title=Here’s why Rutgers checks all of the boxes for Isaiah Crumpler, Greg Schiano’s newest Knight |url=https://www.nj.com/rutgers/2023/05/heres-why-rutgers-checks-all-of-the-boxes-for-isaiah-crumpler-greg-schianos-newest-knight.html |access-date=2025-07-07 |website=nj.com}}</ref><!--A'riana and Isaiah have a mother named Danita (also an ECU alum), but Alge's mother was named Gertha.-->

Crumpler and his wife have three children.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Alge Crumpler '00 - My Carolina Story |url=https://alumni.unc.edu/about-carolina-alumni/gaa-board-of-directors/my-carolina-story/alge-crumpler-my-carolina-story/ |access-date=2025-07-07 |website=UNC Alumni}}</ref> 

After his playing career, Crumpler worked as an analyst for the [[ACC Network (Raycom Sports)|ACC Network]]<ref>{{cite web |date=July 17, 2014 |title=ACC Gridiron Live Presented by McAlister's Deli Debuts August 27 on Fox Sports South |url=http://www.theacc.com/#!/news-detail/ACC-Gridiron-Live-Debut_07-18-14_rqk7v4 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20141123203843/http://www.theacc.com/%23!/news-detail/ACC-Gridiron-Live-Debut_07-18-14_rqk7v4 |archive-date=November 23, 2014 |website=The ACC}}</ref> and a sports radio broadcaster in Atlanta.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-05-20 |title=WQXI Atlanta Drops Local Programming For ESPN |url=https://radioinsight.com/headlines/88704/wqxi-atlanta-drops-local-programming-for-espn/ |access-date=2025-07-07 |website=RadioInsight |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

He played in the NFL primarily with the [[Buffalo Bills]]. Van Pelt previously served as an assistant coach for the Bills, [[Cincinnati Bengals]], [[Green Bay Packers]], [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], [[Cleveland Browns]], [[New England Patriots]], and [[Los Angeles Rams]]. ==Playing career== ===College=== Van Pelt attended the [[University of Pittsburgh]], where he was a four-year starting quarterback for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Panthers]]. When he graduated, Van Pelt broke school career passing records previously set by [[Dan Marino]], holding records for most career passing yards, completions, and attempts in Pitt history.{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/team/coaches-roster/alex-van-pelt |access-date=2024-07-31 |website=www.clevelandbrowns.com |language=en-US}} His single-season mark of 3,163 passing yards in 1992 was broken in 2003 by [[Rod Rutherford]]. *1989: 192/347 for 2,881 yards with 17 touchdowns vs 12 interceptions. Ran for 4 touchdowns. *1990: 201/351 for 2,427 yards with 14 touchdowns vs 17 interceptions. Ran for 2 touchdowns. *1991: 227/398 for 2,796 yards with 15 touchdowns vs 14 interceptions. Ran for 1 touchdown. *1992: 245/407 for 3,163 yards with 20 touchdowns vs 17 interceptions. ===Professional=== {{NFL predraft | height ft = 6 | height in = 0 | weight = 212 | dash = 4.97 | ten split = 1.68 | twenty split = 2.86 | vertical = 30.5 | arm span = 31 7/8 | hand span = 9 3/4 | note = All values from [[NFL Combine]]{{Cite web |url=https://nflcombineresults.com/playerpage.php?f=Alex&l=Van%20Pelt&i=24385 |title=Alex Van Pelt Combine Results |website=NFLCombineResults.com |access-date=June 3, 2026}} }} Van Pelt was an eighth round draft pick of his hometown franchise [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], but was released during [[training camp]].{{Cite web |title=1993 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1993/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} Van Pelt spent three games with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] late in the [[1993 NFL season]] following a hamstring injury to [[Joe Montana]]. He was re-signed by the Chiefs prior to the [[1994 NFL season]], but was released during training camp. He was signed by the [[Buffalo Bills]] later in the 1994 season following a knee injury sustained by [[Jim Kelly]] and spent the remainder of his career as a backup with the Bills.{{cite news|last=Cook|first=Ron|title=Cook: Van Pelt makes mark on Bills|url=http://old.post-gazette.com/sports/columnists/20011226cook1226np1.asp|newspaper=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|access-date=August 25, 2017|archive-date=August 25, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825234719/http://old.post-gazette.com/sports/columnists/20011226cook1226np1.asp|url-status=dead}} Van Pelt's first NFL win as a [[Starting lineup|starter]] would come on November 2, 1997, against [[Dan Marino]] and the [[Miami Dolphins]], playing well enough to justify a contract extension that would allow the Bills to release failed [[Jim Kelly]] successor [[Todd Collins (quarterback)|Todd Collins]]. In [[2001 NFL season|2001]], he started eight games in relief of the injured [[Rob Johnson (American football)|Rob Johnson]], going 2–6. Van Pelt would not start any games after 2001 due to a Bills trade with the [[New England Patriots]] for [[Drew Bledsoe]], who became the full time starting quarterback. Van Pelt remained with the team as Bledsoe's backup for the next two seasons before retiring. In his career, Van Pelt totaled 16 [[touchdown]]s and 24 [[interception]]s on 477 pass attempts in 31 career appearances and 11 starts.{{cite web |title=Alex Van Pelt |url=https://www.nfl.com/player/alexvanpelt/2503454/careerstats |website=nfl.com |access-date=25 February 2020}} ==Broadcasting career== After retiring from football in 2004, Van Pelt was [[John Murphy (announcer)|John Murphy]]'s partner on Bills Radio Network broadcasts. '''Alexander Douglas Smith''' (born May 7, 1984) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[quarterback]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for 16 seasons. He played [[college football]] for the [[Utah Utes football|Utah Utes]], earning first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors and winning [[Mountain West Conference football individual awards#Offensive Player of the Year|MW Offensive Player of the Year]] in 2004. Smith was [[List of first overall NFL draft picks|selected first overall]] by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the [[2005 NFL draft]].

Smith had a breakout season in 2011 when he led the 49ers to their first division title and playoff win since 2002 and their first [[NFC Championship Game]] appearance since 1997. The following season, a concussion resulted in Smith losing his starting position to backup [[Colin Kaepernick]]. Smith was then traded to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] during the offseason and guided them to four playoff runs between 2013 and 2017, their first consecutive division titles in franchise history, and their first playoff victory since 1993 in the 2015 season. Smith also received three [[Pro Bowl]] selections with the Chiefs and led the league in passer rating in 2017. He was traded to the [[Washington Redskins]] in 2018 to make way for second-year quarterback [[Patrick Mahomes]], but was credited with helping develop the future [[National Football League Most Valuable Player Award|NFL MVP]].

During his first season in Washington, Smith suffered a life-threatening injury to his right leg that nearly resulted in amputation. Although expected never to play again, Smith completed a lengthy rehabilitation process that allowed him to return in 2020. Smith became the starter midway through the season, leading the team to a division title and earning [[NFL Comeback Player of the Year]] honors. He retired during the 2021 offseason after being released. Smith's return from injury is cited as among the greatest comeback stories in NFL history.<ref name="ESPNInjury" /> He was inducted to the [[College Football Hall of Fame]] in 2024.

==Early life==
Smith was born on May 7, 1984, in [[Bremerton, Washington]].<ref name=mosher_01202012>{{Cite news |last=Mosher |first=Terry |date=January 20, 2012 |title=Doug Smith brought Olympic to rare heights |url=http://www.kitsapsun.com/news/2012/jan/20/doug-smith-brought-olympic-to-rare-heights/#axzz2XcVsiTAm |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130629153928/http://www.kitsapsun.com/news/2012/jan/20/doug-smith-brought-olympic-to-rare-heights/%23axzz2XcVsiTAm |archive-date=June 29, 2013 |work=Kitsap Sun|quote=Alex Smith, born in Bremerton in 1985, is in his seventh year as the quarterback for the San Francisco 49ers, who continued their remarkable season under first-year coach Jim Harbaugh by stunning the New Orleans Saints in the playoffs last weekend.}}</ref> He grew up in [[La Mesa, California]]. His father, Douglas D. Smith, was an executive director at [[Helix High School]], which Smith attended.<ref name=mosher_01202012/><ref name="It">{{Cite news |last=Ratto |first=Ray |date=April 24, 2005 |title=It's all or nothing for Smith, 49ers |url=http://www.sfgate.com/sports/article/It-s-all-or-nothing-for-Smith-49ers-2639598.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202190823/http://www.sfgate.com/sports/article/It-s-all-or-nothing-for-Smith-49ers-2639598.php |archive-date=February 2, 2014 |access-date=January 20, 2014 |work=San Francisco Chronicle}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Magee |first=Maureen |date=April 30, 2010 |title=Helix High to keep its charter |url=http://www.signonsandiego.com/news/2010/apr/30/helix-high-keep-its-charter/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160827200924/http://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/news/2010/apr/30/helix-high-keep-its-charter/ |archive-date=August 27, 2016 |access-date=April 30, 2010 |website=San Diego Union – Tribune}}</ref>

As a starter for the Helix Highlanders during his junior and senior years, Smith led the team to a 25–1 record, including two San Diego CIF section championships. He was named to the first-team all-conference and all-county squads in the San Diego CIF system. Smith also earned the conference offensive player of the year twice, and twice won the team MVP for Helix. During his time at Helix, Smith set a school record by throwing for six touchdowns in one game, and recorded the second-highest completion percentage in San Diego CIF history. While at Helix, he was teammates with future NFL star [[Reggie Bush]]. Smith and Bush were finalists for the 2004 [[Heisman Trophy]], making it the first time a high school had two finalists at the same ceremony.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Klein |first=Gary |date=December 12, 2004 |title=2 teams have 4 candidates for Heisman |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2004/12/12/2-teams-have-4-candidates-for-heisman/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180312083042/http://articles.chicagotribune.com/2004-12-12/sports/0412120009_1_heisman-ceremony-usc-quarterback-matt-leinart-heisman-officials |archive-date=March 12, 2018 |access-date=March 11, 2018 |website=Chicago Tribune |language=en}}</ref> Bush went on to win the 2005 award.

Smith was president of his senior class in high school, earned college credits through a program at [[San Diego State University]], and took a dozen [[Advanced Placement]] tests.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sullivan |first=Tim |date=April 24, 2005 |title=Alex Smith answers call as top choice by San Francisco 49ers |url=http://www.signonsandiego.com/uniontrib/20050424/news_1s24sullivan.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120125061806/http://www.signonsandiego.com/uniontrib/20050424/news_1s24sullivan.html |archive-date=January 25, 2012 |access-date=September 7, 2007 |website=Sign On San Diego}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Penny |first=La Monica Everett-Haynes and Sharon |date=November 22, 2017 |title=SDSU Guardian Scholars Program Celebrating 10 Years of Support |url=https://www.sdsu.edu/news/2017/11/sdsu-guardian-scholars-program-celebrating-10-years-support |access-date=January 17, 2025 |website=www.sdsu.edu |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mosher |first=Terry |date=December 8, 2020 |title=Smith may have started here, but he's gone far beyond Bremerton |url=https://www.kitsapsun.com/story/sports/2020/12/08/bremerton-born-alex-smith-excels-more-than-just-football-field/6495210002/ |access-date=January 17, 2025 |website=Kitsap Sun |language=en-US}}</ref>

Sports}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===

====2005 season====
The [[San Francisco 49ers]], who held the first overall pick, had hired a head coach with a strong personality in [[Mike Nolan]]. Nolan also evaluated [[University of California, Berkeley|California]] quarterback [[Aaron Rodgers]], but did not believe that Rodgers' attitude could co-exist with him.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peterson |first=Gary |date=January 26, 2011 |title=Peterson: 49ers fans can play fantasy football over Aaron Rodgers vs. Alex Smith and Mike McCarthy vs. Mike Nolan |url=http://www.mercurynews.com/49ers/ci_17199568?nclick_check=1 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121006082237/http://www.mercurynews.com/49ers/ci_17199568?nclick_check=1 |archive-date=October 6, 2012 |access-date=September 2, 2022 |website=San Jose Mercury News |quote=Nolan was no-nonsense, a strong personality who didn't like to be challenged. He met with Rodgers and Smith before the draft. He caught a whiff of attitude from Rodgers, and that was that.}}</ref> Smith was the first overall pick in the [[2005 NFL draft]], selected by the 49ers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2005 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2005/draft.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170921001516/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2005/draft.htm |archive-date=September 21, 2017 |access-date=January 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In July 2005, Smith signed a six-year, $49.5 million contract with $24 million guaranteed.

Dealing with an injury and being taken in and out of the lineup by head coach [[Mike Nolan]], Smith played in nine games as a rookie, throwing for 875 yards, a touchdown, and 11 interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at San Francisco 49ers – January 1st, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200601010sfo.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170709085958/http://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200601010sfo.htm |archive-date=July 9, 2017 |access-date=January 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Smith 2005 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAl03/gamelog/2005/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115220212/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAl03/gamelog/2005/ |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |access-date=January 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2006 season====
After the challenges faced in his rookie campaign, Smith went into the 2006 season with a new offensive coordinator ([[Norv Turner]]) and an improved set of offensive weapons around him. The 49ers used their top draft choice on tight end [[Vernon Davis]]. They also upgraded their offensive backfield, trading underachieving running back [[Kevan Barlow]] to the Jets, making [[Frank Gore]] the feature back.

Smith also spent the off-season working daily with his new coordinator, wide receivers, and tight end while working to improve his technique and add bulk. The improved offensive cast clearly helped Smith develop in his second year, especially early. Smith's first three games of the season saw him throw three touchdowns, no interceptions, and amass 814 yards. After struggling in Kansas City, he then threw for three touchdowns against the [[Oakland Raiders]], setting a career-high.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oakland Raiders at San Francisco 49ers – October 8th, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200610080sfo.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180313093525/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200610080sfo.htm |archive-date=March 13, 2018 |access-date=March 11, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> However, the next five games saw Smith resume his growing pains, averaging only 153 yards per game while throwing only six touchdowns and nine interceptions. Despite his difficulty, he led the 49ers on a three-game winning streak in November.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2006 San Francisco 49ers Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sfo/2006.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180204124007/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sfo/2006.htm |archive-date=February 4, 2018 |access-date=March 11, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Smith met [[Joe Montana]] for the first time on November 5, 2006, during a game against the Vikings. The 49ers wore the throwback jerseys of the 1989 team which Joe Montana and teammates wore. The 49ers went on to win 9–3, upsetting the [[Minnesota Vikings]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers – November 5th, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200611050sfo.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115220208/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200611050sfo.htm |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |access-date=January 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In need of a statement game, the 49ers traveled to Seattle for a ''Thursday Night Football'' game against their division rivals. During the broadcast on NFL Network, [[Cris Collinsworth]] noted that if he were starting an NFL franchise, he would have taken Broncos rookie quarterback [[Jay Cutler]] before Alex Smith and fellow rookies [[Matt Leinart]] and [[Vince Young]] – and that Smith was not even close to the others.<ref name="Maiocco">{{Cite web |last=[[Matt Maiocco]] |title=Matt Maiocco account of SEA vs. SFO game |date=January 8, 1995 |url=http://49ers.pressdemocrat.com/default.asp?item=390733&print=yes/ |archive-url=http://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/20070318012849/http://49ers.pressdemocrat.com/default.asp?item=390733&print=yes%2F |archive-date=March 18, 2007 |access-date=March 16, 2007}}</ref> Going into the 4th quarter, the 49ers were trailing the Seahawks 7–3, and pulling out a win looked unlikely. Smith however performed brilliantly in the fourth quarter, and drove the 49ers on a long touchdown drive down the field early, taking a narrow 10–7 lead. Late in the quarter, with the same score, Smith struck again – shaking off an almost certain sack, rolling to the left and completing a pass to Frank Gore for a touchdown to give the 49ers a 10-point lead. On the next drive, Smith cemented the victory by leading yet another touchdown drive, and rushing for a touchdown on a naked bootleg. Collinsworth had earlier in the game observed that ''"Alex Smith is the best I've ever seen him. That drive is the best I saw,"'' and on seeing his touchdown run, commented ''"What a second-half he has had!"''<ref name=Maiocco/>

After losing to the Cardinals the following week, the 49ers' final game of the 2006 season was against a [[Denver Broncos]] team looking for a playoff berth. In a major upset, the 49ers defeated the Broncos and knocked them out of the playoffs. During the game at [[INVESCO Field]], Smith threw for 194 yards and a touchdown, leading the team to a come from behind victory for the second time in three weeks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Denver Broncos – December 31st, 2006 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200612310den.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115220211/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200612310den.htm |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |access-date=January 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Overall, Smith improved in his second year by throwing as many touchdowns as interceptions. He threw for 16 touchdowns, 16 interceptions, 2,890 yards, and a 74.8 quarterback rating, all improvements over his rookie year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Smith 2006 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAl03/gamelog/2006 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115220157/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAl03/gamelog/2006 |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |access-date=January 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He became the first 49ers quarterback in club history to take every snap from center over the course of a season in 2006.

====2007 season====
Smith entered the 2007 season learning under a third [[offensive coordinator]] in three seasons. [[Norv Turner]] was hired as the [[head coach]] by the [[San Diego Chargers]]. [[Jim Hostler]] replaced Turner. Hostler's system involved a mixture of the offensive system installed by Turner with elements of the [[West Coast offense]] installed by [[Mike McCarthy]] for the 2005 season. During the off-season, the 49ers added [[wide receiver]]s [[Darrell Jackson]], [[Ashley Lelie]], and rookie [[Jason Hill (American football)|Jason Hill]] as new offensive targets for Smith.

In the season opener on ''[[Monday Night Football]]'' against the [[2007 Arizona Cardinals|Arizona Cardinals]], Smith led the 49ers to a 20–17 win in a two-minute comeback. While down 17–13 with less than two minutes left, Smith drove down the field, highlighted by a 25-yard scramble. After the scramble, he threw a 22-yard pass to [[Arnaz Battle]] that was fumbled on the one-yard line, but recovered by a 49er so the ball was placed back on the one-yard line with 26 seconds left. The following play, Battle ran an end-around for the game-winning touchdown. Smith finished the game 15 for 31 with 126 yards and two rushes for 37 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cardinals vs. 49ers – Box Score – September 10, 2007 – ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/boxscore?gameId=270910025 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070917060222/http://scores.espn.go.com/nfl/boxscore?gameId=270910025 |archive-date=September 17, 2007 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

On September 30 in the first quarter of a game against the [[2007 Seattle Seahawks|Seattle Seahawks]], Smith injured his right shoulder after getting sacked by Seahawks defensive tackle [[Rocky Bernard]]. Smith suffered a grade-three separation and the initial diagnosis was that surgery would not be required. Smith missed the next three games before returning to the 49ers' starting lineup on Sunday, October 28, 2007.

The 49ers did not win another game until November 25.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2007 San Francisco 49ers Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sfo/2007.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180313020325/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sfo/2007.htm |archive-date=March 13, 2018 |access-date=March 11, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Among all NFL quarterbacks who qualify for league statistics, only the Jets' [[Kellen Clemens]] had a poorer passer rating than Smith (57.2), Smith completed under 50% of his passes, far below the league average of 60%. Smith was at odds with 49ers head coach [[Mike Nolan]] over the severity of his injury. Nolan publicly implied that Smith was not fighting through the injury, while Smith felt that the injury still affected his ability to throw accurately, an account that was supported by players from the Seahawks.<ref name="rosenthal">{{Cite news |last=Rosenthal |first=Gregg |date=January 22, 2012 |title=They Believed, Smith Delivered |url=http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/46067758/ns/sports-nfl/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120122182558/http://nbcsports.msnbc.com/id/46067758/ns/sports-nfl |archive-date=January 22, 2012 |access-date=January 23, 2012 |publisher=NBC Universal}}</ref><ref name="lynch">{{Cite news |last=Lynch |first=Kevin |date=October 20, 2008 |title=Why Mike Nolan was Fired |url=http://blog.sfgate.com/49ers/2008/10/20/why-mike-nolan-was-fired/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130818183943/http://blog.sfgate.com/49ers/2008/10/20/why-mike-nolan-was-fired/ |archive-date=August 18, 2013 |work=sfgate.com |publisher=[[Hearst Communications]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Player notes |url=http://fantasysports.usatoday.com/content/news.asp?sport=nfl&line=104878 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090508081011/http://fantasysports.usatoday.com/content/news.asp?sport=NFL |archive-date=May 8, 2009 |work=USA Today}}</ref> Nolan decided to rest Smith following a loss in that game to the Seahawks on November 12 and start [[Trent Dilfer]] to allow Smith's shoulder to recover. Following the decision, orthopedic surgeon [[James Andrews (physician)|James Andrews]] said that upon further examination the shoulder did not heal as significantly as Andrews thought it would, and on December 11, 2007, Smith was placed on injured reserve to undergo surgery on the shoulder, ending his season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Smith 2007 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAl03/gamelog/2007 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115214645/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAl03/gamelog/2007 |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |access-date=January 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2008 season====
Smith entered [[Training camp (National Football League)|training camp]] competing for the starting quarterback job with [[Shaun Hill]], who won both of the games he started in 2007, before suffering a back injury against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], and [[Journeyman (sports)|journeyman]] [[J. T. O'Sullivan]]. Smith would be learning under a fourth different offensive coordinator in four seasons; [[Jim Hostler]] was fired and replaced by former [[Detroit Lions]] offensive coordinator and St. Louis Rams offensive coordinator/head coach [[Mike Martz]]. Unlike the previous three seasons, where offensive continuity was somewhat maintained, Martz's system was completely different. Smith lost the starting job in training camp to O'Sullivan,<ref name=espn_09102008/> who was elevated to starting quarterback, partly due to his familiarity with Martz's offense when he was a member of the Detroit Lions.

On September 10, the 49ers placed Smith on [[injured reserve]] after [[James Andrews (physician)|Dr. James Andrews]] confirmed the team's diagnosis of a broken bone in his shoulder,<ref name="espn_09102008">{{Cite web |date=September 10, 2008 |title=Niners QB Smith has broken shoulder, will not play this season |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=3579991 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080912235814/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=3579991 |archive-date=September 12, 2008 |access-date=September 10, 2008 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> believed to have been caused by a wire left in his shoulder from the previous surgery, which had sawed through the bone.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Monson |first=Gordon |date=March 30, 2009 |title=Alex Smith an unanswered question for 49ers |url=http://www.sltrib.com/Sports/ci_12031011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090402011758/http://www.sltrib.com/sports/ci_12031011 |archive-date=April 2, 2009 |access-date=March 31, 2008 |website=The Salt Lake Tribune}}</ref> Regardless, the 49ers' general manager, [[Scot McCloughan]], said that the 49ers expected to release Smith before the 2009 season, when they would owe him a salary of $9,625,000.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 10, 2008 |title=49ers place Smith on injured reserve with broken bone in shoulder |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story?id=09000d5d80ab2163&template=with-video&confirm=true |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080911091052/http://www.nfl.com/news/story?id=09000d5d80ab2163&template=with-video&confirm=true |archive-date=September 11, 2008 |access-date=September 2, 2022 |website=[[NFL.com]]}}</ref>

After Nolan was [[Termination of employment|fired]] on October 20, 2008,<ref name=lynch/> the 49ers expressed interest in having Smith remain for the 2009 season if he was willing to renegotiate his contract.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Crumpacker |first=John |date=August 17, 2010 |title=McCloughan talks up possible return by Smith |url=http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/c/a/2008/11/10/SP8M141JPB.DTL |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090729084648/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=%2Fc%2Fa%2F2008%2F11%2F10%2FSP8M141JPB.DTL |archive-date=July 29, 2009 |work=The San Francisco Chronicle}}</ref> On March 10, 2009, the 49ers announced that his contract had been successfully restructured and that he would stay with the team. He took a considerable pay cut to remain with the 49ers, with whom he would be under contract for the next two years.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 10, 2009 |title=QB Smith agrees to reduced pay to stay in San Francisco |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/football/nfl/03/10/49ers.ap/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090313064351/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/football/nfl/03/10/49ers.ap/index.html |archive-date=March 13, 2009 |access-date=September 20, 2018 |website=SI.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Smith was to make $4 million a season in 2009 and 2010, in addition to base salaries that were not immediately made known. In his previous contract, he was scheduled to make $24.6 million in the final two years.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clayton |first=John |author-link=John Clayton (sportswriter) |date=March 11, 2009 |title=San Francisco 49ers, Alex Smith rework contract |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=3967496 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100816005827/http://sports.espn.go.com/nfl/news/story?id=3967496 |archive-date=August 16, 2010 |access-date=August 4, 2011 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

====2009 season====
[[File:Alex Smith running.jpg|thumb|upright=0.95|Smith in November 2009]]
After the pay cut, Smith said that he was ready to compete for the starting quarterback spot, primarily against [[Shaun Hill]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Killion |first=Ann |date=March 10, 2009 |title=A new beginning for Alex Smith with 49ers |url=http://www.mercurynews.com/sports/ci_11883849 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120927150835/http://www.mercurynews.com/sports/ci_11883849 |archive-date=September 27, 2012 |access-date=March 11, 2009 |website=Mercury News}}</ref>

[[Mike Singletary]] became the head coach after a successful term as the interim head coach in 2008, and Martz was fired as offensive coordinator due to the huge differences in offensive philosophies between himself and Singletary. [[Jimmy Raye II]] was hired to replace him, marking Smith's fifth different offensive coordinator in five seasons. During the off-season, the 49ers drafted [[Michael Crabtree]] to be the featured receiver that Smith had been lacking throughout his NFL career. After restructuring his contract with San Francisco, Smith lost the battle for the starting quarterback position to [[Shaun Hill]]. However, in a Week 7 game against the [[2009 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]], Smith replaced Hill in the third quarter, after Hill had performed poorly and the Niners faced a 21–0 first-half deficit. Smith led the team back with three touchdown passes, all to tight end [[Vernon Davis]], but fell short of victory, 24–21.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rieken |first=Kristie |date=October 25, 2009 |title=Texans hold on to beat 49ers 24–21 |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/recap;_ylt=AqxN7QOWLMaeg2FsmxuFJgBDubYF?gid=20091025034&prov=ap |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120715001705/http://sports.yahoo.com/nfl/recap;_ylt=AqxN7QOWLMaeg2FsmxuFJgBDubYF?gid=20091025034&prov=ap |archive-date=July 15, 2012 |access-date=August 4, 2011 |work=Yahoo! Sports}}</ref> Singletary named Smith as the 49ers' starting quarterback the next day at his weekly press conference on October 26.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Price |first=Taylor |date=October 26, 2009 |title=Singletary Names Smith Starting Quarterback |url=http://blog.49ers.com/2009/10/26/singletary-names-smith-starting-quarterback/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130404044017/http://blog.49ers.com/2009/10/26/singletary-names-smith-starting-quarterback/ |archive-date=2013-04-04 |work=49ers.com |language=en}}</ref>

After his return as the 49ers' starting quarterback, Smith displayed signs of progress, despite the team's 3–4 record in his first seven starts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Daniel |date=December 10, 2009 |title=Jaworski sees improved mechanics for 49ers quarterback Alex Smith | 49ers Hot Read |url=http://blogs.mercurynews.com/49ers/2009/12/10/jaworski-sees-improved-mechanics-for-49ers-quarterback-alex-smith/ |url-status=live yards with two touchdown passes while posting a 96.8 [[passer rating]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 29, 2009 |title=49ers' mistake-free day snaps Jaguars' three-game streak |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=291129025 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110606032313/http://espn.go.com/nfl/recap?gameId=291129025 |archive-date=June 6, 2011 |archive-date=November 2, 2010 |access-date=August 4, 2011 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Overall, he finished the season with 2,350 passing yards, 18 touchdowns, and 12 ====2010 season====
[[File:Alex Smith at 49ers training camp 2010-08-11 1.JPG|thumb|upright=0.95|left|Smith at training camp in 2010]]
Smith entered the 2010 season as the starting quarterback. For the first time in his career, he returned under the same offensive coordinator from the previous season, as Raye was retained. However, continuity in a poor system resulted in the team starting 0–5, and on September 27, Raye was fired and replaced by quarterbacks coach [[Mike Johnson (American football coach)|Mike Johnson]]. Under Johnson, Smith was expected to run a variation of the spread offense that he ran in college. The 49ers continued to build their team having now drafted [[Anthony Davis (offensive tackle b. 1989)|Anthony Davis]] and [[Mike Iupati]] with their two first-round picks to provide more protection. On September 8, Coach Singletary announced that Smith was named one of the team's captains.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 9, 2010 |title=49ers QB Smith earns full-time captain duties |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=5551540 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180312083139/http://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=5551540 |archive-date=March 12, 2018 |access-date=March 11, 2018 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

In Week 5, Smith was booed at home and the crowd chanted for his backup, [[David Carr (American football)|David Carr]], before leading the 49ers to two scoring drives to close within three points. However, he was hit as he threw on the third drive attempt, resulting in an interception and a 24–27 loss, dropping the 49ers to 0–5.<ref>{{Cite news |date=October 10, 2010 |title=Kevin Kolb, Eagles survive as more turnovers keep 49ers winless |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=301010025 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110226053636/http://espn.go.com/nfl/recap?gameId=301010025 |archive-date=February 26, 2011 |work=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Borden |first=Sam |date=January 19, 2012 |title=As a 49er, Carr Saw Alex Smith's Confidence 2010 |access-date=September 2, 2022 |website=[[NFL.com]]}}</ref> in the 49ers week 7<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFL.com Scores |url=http://www.nfl.com/scores/2010/REG7 |url-status=live season|Carolina Panthers]] and was not available to play Week 8 against the [[2010 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]] in London. He was replaced by [[Troy Smith]], who had 14 games of experience in the NFL before joining the 49ers organization just before the start of the regular season. Troy Smith took Smith's position after winning two straight games against the [[2010 St. Louis Rams season|St. Louis Rams]] and the Denver Broncos.<ref>{{Cite web |last=White |first=David |date=October 28, 2010 |title=Troy Smith replaces Alex Smith as 49ers' QB |url=https://www.sfgate.com/49ers/article/Troy-Smith-replaces-Alex-Smith-as-49ers-QB-3248287.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220902174951/https://www.sfgate.com/49ers/article/Troy-Smith-replaces-Alex-Smith-as-49ers-QB-3248287.php |archive-date=September 2, 2022 |access-date=September 2, 2022 |website=SFGATE |language=en-US}}</ref>

However, following a loss to the [[2010 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]] in Week 13 that left the 49ers with a 4–8 record, Troy Smith was demoted to backup in favor of Alex Smith. Smith would start against the [[2010 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]] in Week 14 in a game the 49ers needed to win to stay in contention in the NFC West.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 San Francisco 49ers Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sfo/2010.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115214647/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sfo/2010.htm |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |access-date=January 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Smith acknowledged that his performances needed to be more consistent.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Brown |first=Daniel |date=December 8, 2010 |title=San Francisco 49ers' Alex Smith won't stop believing ... in himself |url=http://www.mercurynews.com/sports-headlines/ci_16812047?nclick_check=1 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130819143205/http://www.mercurynews.com/sports-headlines/ci_16812047?nclick_check=1 |archive-date=August 19, 2013 |work=[[San Jose Mercury News]]}}</ref> On December 12, 2010, the 49ers played the Seahawks in San Francisco. Smith was booed by the Candlestick crowd after the first two plays. However, the boos turned to cheers after Smith helped lead the 49ers to a 40–21 victory over a division rival.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers – December 12th, 2010 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201012120sfo.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115220209/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201012120sfo.htm |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |access-date=January 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The win moved the 49ers one game behind the division leaders (Rams and Seahawks) with three games left to play. However, the 49ers struggled the following Thursday night against the [[2010 San Diego Chargers season|San Diego Chargers]] and Troy Smith started the following game against the Rams. Troy Smith struggled in the loss to the Rams and Alex relieved Troy Smith in that game. After the game, Singletary was fired and Alex finished the season starting against the Cardinals. The 49ers finished the season 6–10 and Smith became a free agent after the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 San Francisco 49ers Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sfo/2010.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115214647/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sfo/2010.htm |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |access-date=March 11, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> After his firing, Singletary said, "You gotta have a quarterback."<ref name=rosenthal/> Smith had won just 19 games in 50 career starts through 2010.<ref>{{Cite news |date=January 21, 2012 |title=QBs rewriting history on Sunday |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/statsinfo/post/_/id/37088/qbs-re-writing-history-on-sunday |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120123171900/http://espn.go.com/blog/statsinfo/post/_/id/37088/qbs-re-writing-history-on-sunday |archive-date=January 23, 2012 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref>

====2011 season====
The 49ers hired [[Jim Harbaugh]] as the new head coach, and [[Greg Roman]] replaced Johnson as the new offensive coordinator.<ref name="fox">{{Cite news |last=Fox |first=Ashley |date=January 18, 2012 |title=Alex Smith has the 49ers in good hands |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/7475573/jim-harbaugh-faith-alex-smith-paid-49ers |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120120163434/http://espn.go.com/nfl/story/_/id/7475573/jim-harbaugh-faith-alex-smith-paid-49ers |archive-date=January 20, 2012 |work=ESPN.com}}</ref> Harbaugh made it known to Smith that he was welcomed back on the team. Smith's family wanted him to leave San Francisco.<ref name=rosenthal/> Although he was unsigned, Smith organized the players' workouts during the [[2011 NFL lockout]] and helped to install Harbaugh's new offense.<ref name="brown">{{Cite news |last=Brown |first=Daniel |date=January 21, 2012 |title=49ers' magic run had beginnings at Camp Alex |url=http://www.mercurynews.com/49ers/ci_19785290 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130819113538/http://www.mercurynews.com/49ers/ci_19785290 |archive-date=August 19, 2013 |work=San Jose Mercury News}}</ref> After the lockout ended, Smith signed a one-year $5 million contract with the 49ers.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Killion |first=Ann |date=August 1, 2011 |title=New era begins for 49ers, but will San Francisco get any better? |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/writers/ann_killion/08/01/49ers/?sct=hp_t11_a4 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130819155911/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2011/writers/ann_killion/08/01/49ers/?sct=hp_t11_a4 |archive-date=August 19, 2013 |work=SI.com}}</ref><ref name="2011starter">{{Cite news |date=September 2, 2011 |title=Alex Smith named starter for 49ers |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/6922974/san-francisco-49ers-name-alex-smith-starting-qb |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110929061713/http://espn.go.com/nfl/story/_/id/6922974/san-francisco-49ers-name-alex-smith-starting-qb |archive-date=September 29, 2011 |access-date=September 2, 2011 |work=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Smith was named the starting quarterback heading into the regular season, and Harbaugh believed Smith could succeed in the coach's West Coast offense.<ref name=2011starter/>

During the season, Smith's game showed marked improvement, especially in his leadership and intangibles. While he did not put up big numbers, he helped the 49ers win games through efficient play, minimizing mistakes and controlling the clock. In a road game against the [[2011 Philadelphia Eagles season|Philadelphia Eagles]] in Week 4, Smith rallied the team from a 23–3 second-half deficit to win 24–23, completing 9 of 9 passes for 179 yards and two touchdowns in the third quarter alone.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Philadelphia Eagles – October 2nd, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201110020phi.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108204447/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201110020phi.htm |archive-date=November 8, 2017 |access-date=January 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Two weeks later, Smith led his third come-from-behind road victory of the year with a six-yard fourth and goal touchdown pass to tight end Delanie Walker, beating the [[2011 Detroit Lions season|Lions]] in Detroit 25–19.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Detroit Lions – October 16th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201110160det.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107083552/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201110160det.htm |archive-date=November 7, 2017 |access-date=January 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In a week 10 matchup against the [[2011 New York Giants season|New York Giants]], he completed 19 out of 30 passes for 242 yards. The Giants shut down the 49ers' run game (Frank Gore was held to zero yards on six carries before leaving the game in the second half) and Smith was instrumental in the 27–20 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Giants at San Francisco 49ers – November 13th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201111130sfo.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115214649/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201111130sfo.htm |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |access-date=January 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

By the time the 2011 season was finished, Smith had helped lead the 49ers to a 13–3 record in the regular season, including five come-from-behind victories in which four were on the road, and the 49ers earned a first-round bye in the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2011 San Francisco 49ers Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sfo/2011.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170804014249/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sfo/2011.htm |archive-date=August 4, 2017 |access-date=March 11, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> After 3 head coaches, 7 offensive coordinators, and 17 different starting wide receivers in the span of 7 seasons with the 49ers,<ref name=rosenthal/> Smith would finally make his first playoff appearance.

In the [[2011–12 NFL playoffs#NFC: San Francisco 49ers 36, New Orleans Saints 32|Divisional Round]], Smith led the 49ers to a 36–32 victory over the [[2011 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]]. He threw for 299 yards, three touchdowns, and no interceptions while rushing for an additional touchdown. Smith led touchdown drives of 80 and 85 yards in the final 4:02.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ortiz |first=Jorge L. |date=January 15, 2012 |title=TD could become 'The Catch III' in 49ers lore |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/football/nfl/niners/story/2012-01-15/vernon-davis-alex-smith-catch/52587252/1 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120116094013/http://www.usatoday.com/sports/football/nfl/niners/story/2012-01-15/vernon-davis-alex-smith-catch/52587252/1 |archive-date=January 16, 2012 |work=[[USA Today]] |publisher=David Hunke; [[Gannett Company]]}}</ref> He scored on a 28-yard touchdown run, and he threw a game-winning 14-yard touchdown pass to [[Vernon Davis]] with nine seconds remaining, eschewing a more conservative open receiver that would have settled for a field goal and a tie.<ref name=brown/><ref>{{Cite news |last=Benoit |first=Andy |date=January 16, 2012 |title=Quick Hits: Alex Smith Trusts His Arm |url=http://fifthdown.blogs.nytimes.com/2012/01/16/quick-hits-alex-smith-trusts-his-arm/?scp=1&sq=%22alex%20smith%22&st=cse |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150610232906/http://fifthdown.blogs.nytimes.com/2012/01/16/quick-hits-alex-smith-trusts-his-arm/?scp=1&sq=%22alex%20smith%22&st=cse |archive-date=June 10, 2015 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> Analyst [[Ron Jaworski]] said "Alex Smith won the game, not Alex Smith by not making mistakes. ====2012 season====
[[File:Alex Smith - San Francisco vs Green Bay 2012 (4).jpg|thumb|left|upright=0.85|Smith warming up for the 2012 season opener]]

Smith became a free agent following the 2011 season. The 49ers were reported to be interested in signing [[Peyton Manning]], who had just been released by the rebuilding [[Indianapolis Colts]], leading Smith to visit the [[Miami Dolphins]], reportedly with the intent to sign with the Dolphins if the 49ers signed Manning. Shortly after Manning decided to join the [[Denver Broncos]], Smith signed a three-year contract worth $24 million to remain with the 49ers.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Branch |first=Eric |date=March 21, 2012 |title=Alex Smith, 49ers agree to 3 years, 24 million |url=http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/c/a/2012/03/20/SP1N1NNIQJ.DTL |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120321081637/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=%2Fc%2Fa%2F2012%2F03%2F20%2FSP1N1NNIQJ.DTL |archive-date=March 21, 2012 |work=The San Francisco Chronicle}}</ref> During the offseason, the 49ers added wide receivers [[Randy Moss]] and [[Mario Manningham]] in free agency, and [[A. J. Jenkins]] in the first round of the [[2012 NFL draft]] to improve a passing game that lacked production from the receivers the previous season. Smith began the 2012 season as the starting quarterback. Smith completed 18-of-19 passes for 232 yards and three touchdowns without an interception in a 24–3 Monday night victory over Arizona, and San Francisco was 6–2 after eight games.<ref name="branch">{{Cite news |last=Branch |first=John |date=January 11, 2013 |title=Teacher's Grade Hinges on Student's Playoff Test |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/01/12/sports/football/with-49ers-teachers-grade-hinges-on-students-playoff-test.html?_r=0 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150403233430/http://www.nytimes.com/2013/01/12/sports/football/with-49ers-teachers-grade-hinges-on-students-playoff-test.html?_r=0 |archive-date=April 3, 2015 |access-date=January 14, 2013 |work=The New York Times}}</ref> In the next game against the [[2012 St. Louis Rams season|St. Louis Rams]], Smith suffered a concussion in the second quarter, throwing a touchdown with blurred vision before exiting the game. He was replaced by [[Colin Kaepernick]], and the game ended in a 24–24 tie.<ref name=colin_first_team/>

Smith missed the following game, and Kaepernick was 16 of 23 for 243 yards with two touchdowns in a 32–7 victory over the [[2012 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]].<ref ===Kansas City Chiefs===

====2013 season====
On February 27, 2013, the 49ers agreed to trade Smith to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] for the Chiefs' second round pick in the [[2013 NFL draft]] and a conditional pick in the [[2014 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 12, 2013 |title=49ers Acquire Picks in Alex Smith Trade |url=http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/49ers-Acquire-Picks-in-Alex-Smith-Trade/8c8998c0-9559-42b7-85ef-fa6997442a8a |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130316055512/http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/49ers-Acquire-Picks-in-Alex-Smith-Trade/8c8998c0-9559-42b7-85ef-fa6997442a8a |archive-date=March 16, 2013 |access-date=March 31, 2013 |website=49ers.com}}</ref> The deal became official at the beginning of the new league year on March 12.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=March 12, 2013 |title=Alex Smith-to-Chiefs trade now official - ProFootballTalk.com |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/03/12/alex-smith-to-chiefs-trade-now-official/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130314233543/http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/03/12/alex-smith-to-chiefs-trade-now-official/ |archive-date=March 14, 2013}}</ref>

After the trade became official, Chiefs head coach [[Andy Reid]] stated that Smith would be the starting quarterback for the 2013 season. Smith's job as the starter was solidified during OTA's (Organized Team Activities, a term usually referring to NFL pre-season activities). According to coaches and teammates, Smith displayed a very high "football IQ," and his accuracy in passing was lauded as the best many had ever seen. According to Kansas City's quarterbacks coach, Smith was "super intelligent" and had all of the intangibles that he looked for in a quarterback.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 19, 2013 |title=Chiefs Q & A: Quarterbacks Coach Matt Nagy |url=http://www.kcchiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Q--A-Quarterbacks-Coach-Matt-Nagy/c64445f4-64ba-4efd-8baf-b7c780f1d81b |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130802091511/http://www.kcchiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Q--A-Quarterbacks-Coach-Matt-Nagy/c64445f4-64ba-4efd-8baf-b7c780f1d81b |archive-date=August 2, 2013 |access-date=August 24, 2013 |website=Kansas City Chiefs}}</ref> The Chiefs were the last unbeaten team in the 2013 NFL season with Smith winning his first nine regular-season starts, gaining 1,919 passing yards with nine touchdowns compared to four interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Smith 11; Quarterback; Kansas City Chiefs (Player profile) |url=http://msn.foxsports.com/nfl/player/alex-smith/300049?q%3Dalex-smith |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131010090353/http://msn.foxsports.com/nfl/player/alex-smith/300049?q=alex-smith |archive-date=October 10, 2013 |access-date=October 28, 2013 |website=MSN.FoxSports.com}}</ref> Smith earned his first and only [[perfect passer rating]] on December 15, 2013. He was 17 of 20 with 287 yards and 5 touchdowns, four of them going to [[Jamaal Charles]], in a victory over the [[2013 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs at Oakland Raiders – December 15th, 2013 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201312150rai.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115220159/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201312150rai.htm |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |access-date=January 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Smith and the Chiefs lost to [[Andrew Luck]] and the [[2013 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] in the AFC [[2013–14 NFL playoffs#AFC: Indianapolis Colts 45, Kansas City Chiefs 44|Wild Card Round]] – on January 4, 2014. Smith threw four touchdowns, completing 30 of his 46 pass attempts for 378 yards and no interceptions, while also carrying the ball 8 times for 57 yards. However, he did commit his team's only turnover, losing a fumble. The final score of the game was 45–44 in favor of the Colts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card – Kansas City Chiefs at Indianapolis Colts – January 4th, 2014 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201401040clt.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170904065457/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201401040clt.htm |archive-date=September 4, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

Smith was elected to his first [[Pro Bowl]] at the end of the season as a replacement for [[Tom Brady]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Alper |first=Josh |date=January 21, 2014 |title=Alex Smith in, Tom Brady out for Pro Bowl |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/01/21/alex-smith-in-tom-brady-out-for-pro-bowl/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140122110813/http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/01/21/alex-smith-in-tom-brady-out-for-pro-bowl/ |archive-date=January 22, 2014 |access-date=January 15, 2021 |website=ProFootballTalk}}</ref> In [[2014 Pro Bowl|the game]], Smith led all quarterbacks in yards, tied for most touchdowns, and led the game-winning touchdown drive at the end of the game that resulted in him throwing a touchdown pass to [[DeMarco Murray]] for a 22–21 win.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garcia |first=Oskar |date=January 26, 2014 |title=Chiefs QB Alex Smith leads comeback as Team Rice beats Team Sanders 22–21 in schoolyard-format Pro Bowl |url=http://www.kansascity.com/2014/01/26/4778550/chiefs-qb-alex-smith-leads.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222140108/http://www.kansascity.com/2014/01/26/4778550/chiefs-qb-alex-smith-leads.html |archive-date=February 22, 2014 |access-date=February 12, 2014 |website=The Kansas City Star|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

====2014 season====
[[File:Alex Smith 2014 Pro Bowl.jpg|thumb|Smith during the [[2014 Pro Bowl]]]]
On August 31, 2014, Smith and the Chiefs agreed to a four-year contract extension.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Paylor |first=Terez A. |date=August 31, 2014 |title=Chiefs reach new four-year deal with quarterback Alex Smith |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/article1336989.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140901111028/http://www.kansascity.com/sports/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/article1336989.html |archive-date=September 1, 2014 |access-date=August 31, 2014 |website=The Kansas City Star}}</ref> Smith appeared in 15 games and completed 65.3% of his passes in the 2014 season while throwing for 3,265 yards and 18 touchdowns to only six interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Smith 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAl03/gamelog/2014/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171115020617/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAl03/gamelog/2014/ |archive-date=November 15, 2017 |access-date=November 14, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> However, the Chiefs finished with a 9–7 record and did not qualify for the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2014 Kansas City Chiefs Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/kan/2014.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171115015504/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/kan/2014.htm |archive-date=November 15, 2017 |access-date=November 14, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2015 season====
After another strong season in 2015, Smith was elected to the Pro Bowl as an alternate, but turned down the offer. He once again led the Chiefs to the playoffs, where they defeated the [[2015 Houston Texans season|Houston Texans]] 30–0 in the [[2015–16 NFL playoffs#AFC: Kansas City Chiefs 30, Houston Texans 0|Wild Card Round]]. Smith threw for 190 yards, a touchdown, and an interception in the victory over the Texans. He also rushed five times for 27 yards and had a 64-yard scramble that was called back due to a holding penalty.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card – Kansas City Chiefs at Houston Texans – January 9th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201601090htx.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171116035220/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201601090htx.htm |archive-date=November 16, 2017 |access-date=November 15, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The Chiefs went on to lose 27–20 against the [[2015 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] in the [[2015–16 NFL playoffs#AFC: New England Patriots 27, Kansas City Chiefs 20|Divisional Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Kansas City Chiefs at New England Patriots – January 16th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201601160nwe.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171226094852/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201601160nwe.htm |archive-date=December 26, 2017 |access-date=January 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The Chiefs became the first team ever to start the season 1–5 and win a playoff game. At the end of the season, ''Sports Illustrated'' named Smith the best-looking quarterback in the NFL, an honor previously won by Tom Brady.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Wertheim |first1=Jon |last2=Sommers |first2=Sam |date=February 2, 2016 |title=What's behind attractiveness in NFL quarterbacks? |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2016/02/02/nfl-quarterbacks-attractive-your-brain-on-sports |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170710140633/https://www.si.com/nfl/2016/02/02/nfl-quarterbacks-attractive-your-brain-on-sports |archive-date=July 10, 2017 |access-date=January 15, 2021 |website=SI.com}}</ref> He was named team MVP for 2015 alongside safety [[Eric Berry]]. In the regular season, Smith threw for 3,486 yards, 20 touchdowns, and only seven interceptions, with a completion percentage of 65.3, a passer rating of 95.4, and 7.4 yards per attempt. He also rushed 84 times for 498 yards, two touchdowns, and an average of 5.9 yards per carry.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Smith 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAl03/gamelog/2015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180115220214/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAl03/gamelog/2015 |archive-date=January 15, 2018 |access-date=January 15, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> At the end of the season, Smith was recognized as the 81st best player by his peers on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2016]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2016 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2016-nfl-top-100.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108032657/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2016-nfl-top-100.htm |archive-date=January 8, 2021 |access-date=September 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>
====2016 season====
[[File:Col. Lorenzo Bradley takes a selfie with Alex Smith (3016277) (cropped).jpg|left|thumb|Smith in 2016]]During the season opener, Smith led a fourth quarter comeback over the [[2016 San Diego Chargers season|San Diego Chargers]] to win the game 33–27 in overtime after facing a 24–3 third quarter deficit. Smith won the game in overtime with a two-yard rushing touchdown. This became the largest comeback victory in franchise history as the Chiefs started the season on a positive note.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs Biggest Comebacks |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/kan/comebacks.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909004339/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/kan/comebacks.htm |archive-date=September 9, 2017 |access-date=September 8, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> In 2016, Smith posted a career-high passing yards with 3,502 and a career-high 328 completions despite missing one game. He also ran for a career-high five touchdowns, with three of them coming in the last three games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Smith 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAl03/gamelog/2016/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170908201357/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAl03/gamelog/2016/ |archive-date=September 8, 2017 |access-date=September 8, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> Smith helped lead the Chiefs to the postseason, where they lost to the [[2016 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]] in the [[2016–17 NFL playoffs#AFC: Pittsburgh Steelers 18, Kansas City Chiefs 16|Divisional Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Pittsburgh Steelers at Kansas City Chiefs – January 15th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701150kan.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180106173254/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201701150kan.htm |archive-date=January 6, 2018 |access-date=June 26, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was ranked 81st by his fellow players, for the second consecutive year, on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2017]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2017-nfl-top-100.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220511024213/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2017-nfl-top-100.htm |archive-date=May 11, 2022 |access-date=September 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Washington Redskins / Football Team===
====2018 season====
On January 30, 2018, Smith was traded to the [[Washington Redskins]] in exchange for cornerback [[Kendall Fuller]] and a third-round pick (78th overall) in the [[2018 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Paylor |first=Terez A. |date=January 30, 2018 |title=Chiefs trade Alex Smith to Washington, saving $15.6 million |url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/article197508249.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180131032909/http://www.kansascity.com/sports/nfl/kansas-city-chiefs/article197508249.html |archive-date=January 31, 2018 |access-date=January 31, 2018 |work=The Kansas City Star}}</ref> The trade became official on March 14, the first day of the new league year.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Czarda |first=Stephen |date=March 14, 2018 |title=Redskins Trade For Pro Bowl Quarterback Alex Smith |url=http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Trade-For-Pro-Bowl-Quarterback-Alex-Smith/57ac4989-abae-444b-bb6f-194fa4a9db51 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180314234311/http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Trade-For-Pro-Bowl-Quarterback-Alex-Smith/57ac4989-abae-444b-bb6f-194fa4a9db51 |archive-date=March 14, 2018 |access-date=March 14, 2018 |website=Redskins.com}}</ref> Smith subsequently signed a four-year, $94 million contract extension with the Redskins.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Axson |first=Scooby |date=March 19, 2018 |title=Report: Redskins QB Alex Smith Signs Extension; To Make $40 Million in 2018 |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2018/03/19/washington-redskins-alex-smith-contract |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180907032305/https://www.si.com/nfl/2018/03/19/washington-redskins-alex-smith-contract |archive-date=September 7, 2018 |access-date=September 7, 2018 |website=SI.com}}</ref>

During his Redskins debut, Smith threw for 255 yards and two touchdowns in a 24–6 road victory over the [[2018 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Washington Redskins at Arizona Cardinals – September 9th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201809090ari.htm |access-date=September 10, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=September 9, 2018 |title=New Redskins QB Alex Smith leads Washington to victory over Arizona |url=http://www.fox5dc.com/sports/new-redskins-qb-alex-smith-leads-washington-to-victory-over-arizona |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181002180842/http://www.fox5dc.com/sports/new-redskins-qb-alex-smith-leads-washington-to-victory-over-arizona |archive-date=October 2, 2018 |access-date=October 2, 2018 |website=WTTG |language=en-US |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Through the first nine games of the season, he helped lead Washington to a 6–3 record.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alex Smith 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAl03/gamelog/2018/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181001213634/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAl03.htm |archive-date=October 1, 2018 |access-date=January 23, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>
