==Personal life==
Dennard's last name is pronounced as DENN-erd. His [[second cousin]] [[Darqueze Dennard]] was also an NFL cornerback, although Darqueze pronounces his last name de-NARD, due to a family dispute between his parents.<ref name="n594">{{cite web | last=Bennett | first=Brian | title=Q&A: Michigan State's Darqueze Dennard | website=ESPN.com | date=2013-10-04 | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/bigten/post/_/id/85493/qa-michigan-states-darqueze-dennard | access-date=2024-12-26}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Skinner|first1=Richard|title=How do you pronounce Dennard?|url=http://www.cincinnati.com/story/blogs/2014/10/03/bengals-pats-cb-related-but-dont-pronounce-name-same/16653389/|website=Cincinnati.com|publisher=Gannett Company|access-date=May 7, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150507152811/http://www.cincinnati.com/story/blogs/2014/10/03/bengals-pats-cb-related-but-dont-pronounce-name-same/16653389/|archive-date=May 7, 2015}}</ref>

===Legal troubles===
On April 21, 2012, Dennard was arrested for felony suspicion of assault on a police officer and felony assault in Lincoln, Nebraska. On February 20, 2013, he was convicted of felony assault on a police officer.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/patriots/2013/02/20/patriots-dennard-guilty-of-assaulting-officer/1933147/|title=Pats' Alfonzo Dennard convicted of assaulting officer|access-date=February 24, 2013|date=February 20, 2013|newspaper=USA Today}}</ref> On April 11, 2013, he received his sentence for the assault and was sentenced to 30 days in jail beginning on March 1, 2014, and two years of probation.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Yates |first=Field |author-link=Field Yates |date=2013-04-11 |title=Pats' Dennard gets 30 days in jail in 2014 |url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nfl/story/_/id/9159430/alfonzo-dennard-new-england-patriots-gets-30-days-jail-2014 |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> On July 11, 2013,  Dennard was arrested on suspicion of a DUI and admitted to this probation violation at a later court hearing. He was scheduled for a sentencing hearing on December 5, 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.omaha.com/2013/09/16/alfonzo-dennard-admits-probation-violation/|title=Alfonzo Dennard admits probation violation|last=McKewon|first=Sam|publisher=Omaha Herald|date=September 16, 2013|access-date=September 16, 2013|archive-date=January 13, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140113081209/http://sports.omaha.com/2013/09/16/alfonzo-dennard-admits-probation-violation/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 5, 2013, he attended his sentencing hearing for the probation violation in connection with the DUI and was sentenced to an additional 30 days in jail, was, required to perform 100 hours of community service, received an additional year of probation, and was given a "no alcohol" condition.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/eye-on-football/24350165/patriots-cb-alfonzo-dennard-sentenced-to-extra-30-days-in-jail|title=Patriots CB Alfonzo Dennard sentenced to extra 30 days in jail|last=Katzowitz|first=Josh|date=December 5, 2013|access-date=January 21, 2014|publisher=CBSsports.com}}</ref> On March 1, 2014, Dennard reported to the Lancaster County Adult Detention Facility in Nebraska to begin serving his 60-day jail term.<ref name="jail">{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nfl/story/_/id/10537279/alfonzo-dennard-new-england-patriots-reports-nebraska-jail |title=Alfonzo Dennard reports to Neb. jail |agency=[[Associated Press]] |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=March 1, 2014 |access-date=March 1, 2014}}</ref> He served the minimum 35 days and was released after given credit for good behavior and time already served.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/new-england-patriots-alfonzo-dennard-released-from-jail-0ap2000000339621|title=New England Patriots' Alfonzo Dennard released from jail|last=Maquinana|first=Ryan|date=April 5, 2014|access-date=September 24, 2014|work=NFL.com}}</ref>

On December 15, 2015, it was reported that Dennard had spent five days in Lancaster County Jail after violating the terms of his probation the week prior. He violated the terms after failing tests for alcohol three times in a single month and failed to appear for another drug test.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 15, 2015 |title=Ex-Patriot Alfonzo Dennard jailed for five days |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/2015/12/16/patriot-alfonzo-dennard-set-jail/gHphoMIfoZvXy5cc8rxzNN/story.html?outputType=amp |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=The Boston Globe|agency=Associated Press |language=en-US}}</ref>

Dennard was arrested again in Lincoln, NE on February 9, 2022, for alleged third degree assault and domestic violence.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://klin.com/2022/02/10/former-husker-alfonzo-dennard-booked-for-domestic-assault/|title=Former Husker Alfonzo Dennard Booked for Domestic Assault|last=Henry|first=Kaleb|date=February 10, 2022|access-date=February 11, 2022|publisher=KLIN.com}}</ref>

'''Alfred Bruce Morris''' (born December 12, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Florida Atlantic Owls football|Florida Atlantic Owls]] and was selected by the [[Washington Redskins]] in the sixth round of the [[2012 NFL draft]]. Morris also played for the [[San Francisco 49ers]], [[Dallas Cowboys]], [[Arizona Cardinals]], and [[New York Giants]].
{{TOClimit|limit=3}}

==Early life==
Morris attended [[Pine Forest High School]] in [[Pensacola, Florida]], where he was a letterman in [[high school football|football]], [[basketball]], and [[track and field|track]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alfred Morris Bio |url=http://www.fausports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/morris_alfred00.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150912112002/http://www.fausports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/morris_alfred00.html |archive-date=September 12, 2015 |access-date=April 1, 2016 |website=FAU Owls Athletics}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Vilano |first=Bill |date=January 6, 2016 |title=Pine Forest grad Alfred Morris part of Redskins hopes |url=https://www.pnj.com/story/sports/football/2016/01/06/pine-forest-grad-morris-finding-past-form-right-time/78362342/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180302045309/https://www.pnj.com/story/sports/football/2016/01/06/pine-forest-grad-morris-finding-past-form-right-time/78362342/ |archive-date=March 2, 2018 |access-date=March 1, 2018 |website=Pensacola News Journal |language=en}}</ref> In football, Morris saw action on both sides of the ball. As a senior, he rushed for 1,049 yards with 17 [[touchdown]]s and added 147 tackles and five interceptions on defense.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=December 23, 2014 |title=Cowboys Extra: Spotlight on Redskins running back Alfred Morris |url=http://www.star-telegram.com/sports/nfl/dallas-cowboys/article4900788.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180302103927/http://www.star-telegram.com/sports/nfl/dallas-cowboys/article4900788.html |archive-date=March 2, 2018 |access-date=March 1, 2018 |website=Star-Telegram |language=en}}</ref> Morris was named North West Florida MVP, first-team All-State and was a game MVP. He also participated in the PSA All-Star Game. Academically, Morris was named the student-athlete of the month for Pine Forest. When he was in the sixth grade, Morris played youth football against future Pensacola football stars, wide receiver [[Doug Baldwin]], and running back [[Trent Richardson]]. Morris and Richardson met again in their rookie seasons as the Redskins would travel to Cleveland to take on the Browns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Heist |first=Bob |date=December 16, 2012 |title=Trent, Alfred meet for first time in NFL |url=http://www.pnj.com/article/20121216/SPORTS/312160033/Trent-Alfred-meet-first-time-NFL |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121217201322/http://www.pnj.com/article/20121216/SPORTS/312160033/Trent-Alfred-meet-first-time-NFL |archive-date=December 17, 2012 |access-date=December 23, 2012 |website=Pensacola News Journal}}</ref>

In track, Morris was one of the state's top performers in the jumping events. At the 2007 FHSAA 1A-2A Outdoor State Finals, he earned a tenth-place finish in the [[triple jump]] event, after clearing a career-best mark of 13.40 meters.<ref>{{Cite web |title=FHSAA 1A-2A Outdoor State Finals – 2A Complete Results (Raw) |url=http://fl.milesplit.com/meets/21200/results/46741 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150701231141/http://fl.milesplit.com/meets/21200/results/46741 |archive-date=July 1, 2015 |access-date=April 1, 2016 |website=Fl.milesplit.com}}</ref> Morris also got a PR of 6.48 meters in the [[long jump]] and ran the [[200 meters]] in 23.46 seconds.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alfred Morris {{pipe}} Florida Atlantic {{pipe}} Redskins RB |url=https://www.trackingfootball.com/players/alfred-morris-8644/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304042306/https://www.trackingfootball.com/players/alfred-morris-8644/ |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |access-date=April 1, 2016 |website=Trackingfootball.com}}</ref>

Morris attended and played college football for Florida Atlantic from 2008 to 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alfred Morris College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alfred-morris-1.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180302044825/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alfred-morris-1.html |archive-date=March 2, 2018 |access-date=March 1, 2018 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys (first stint)===

====2016 season====
On March 22, 2016, Morris signed a two-year, $3.5 million contract with the [[Dallas Cowboys]], with the potential to earn up to $5.5 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=March 22, 2016 |title=Cowboys sign Alfred Morris on two-year, $3.5M deal |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/cowboys-sign-alfred-morris-on-two-year-3-5m-deal-0ap3000000646487 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160322220240/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000646487/article/cowboys-sign-alfred-morris-on-twoyear-35m-deal |archive-date=March 22, 2016 |access-date=March 22, 2016 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> The Cowboys were looking to improve their running back production from the previous year and also drafted [[Ezekiel Elliott]] in the first round on April 28. With the emergence of Elliott who became the league's leading rusher, Morris was mostly used on third downs and was forced to focus on his blocking and receiving skills.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Benne |first=Jon |date=April 28, 2016 |title=Elliott drafted by Cowboys |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2016/4/28/11329498/ezekiel-elliott-nfl-draft-dallas-cowboys |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190204065723/https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2016/4/28/11329498/ezekiel-elliott-nfl-draft-dallas-cowboys |archive-date=February 4, 2019 |access-date=February 3, 2019 |website=SBNation.com}}</ref>

On September 11, 2016, Morris made his Cowboys debut, running for 35 yards on seven carries in a 20–19 loss to the [[2016 New York Giants|New York Giants]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 11, 2016 |title=Cowboys' Ezekiel Elliott: Held in check in NFL debut |url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/cowboys-ezekiel-elliott-held-in-check-in-nfl-debut/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161121103338/http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/cowboys-ezekiel-elliott-held-in-check-in-nfl-debut/ |archive-date=November 21, 2016 |access-date=November 20, 2016 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref> On September 18, 2016, Morris scored his first touchdown of the season against the [[2016 Washington Redskins season|Washington Redskins]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dallas Cowboys at Washington Redskins - September 18th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609180was.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190412124810/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609180was.htm |archive-date=April 12, 2019 |access-date=October 4, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On September 25, 2016, Morris scored his second touchdown of the season against the [[2016 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Scott |first=Jim |date=September 25, 2016 |title=Morris Runs It In [Video] |url=http://www.bloggingtheboys.com/2016/9/25/13053748/cowboys-alfred-morris-scores-another-rushing-touchdown-for-dallas |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161121044619/http://www.bloggingtheboys.com/2016/9/25/13053748/cowboys-alfred-morris-scores-another-rushing-touchdown-for-dallas |archive-date=November 21, 2016 |access-date=November 20, 2016 |website=Blogging The Boys}}</ref> On November 6, 2016, Morris ran for a season-high 56 yards on 17 carries against the [[2016 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Halprin |first=Dave |date=November 6, 2016 |title=Cowboys @ Browns: 6 Winners & 3 Losers |url=http://www.bloggingtheboys.com/2016/11/6/13544264/dallas-cowboys-cleveland-browns-6-winners-3-losers-dak-prescott-ezekiel-elliott-dez-bryant-tony-romo |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161121103558/http://www.bloggingtheboys.com/2016/11/6/13544264/dallas-cowboys-cleveland-browns-6-winners-3-losers-dak-prescott-ezekiel-elliott-dez-bryant-tony-romo |archive-date=November 21, 2016 |access-date=November 20, 2016 |website=Blogging The Boys|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> In Week 15, he was passed on the depth chart after the Cowboys activated [[Darren McFadden]] from the non-football injury list. He was declared inactive against the [[2016 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] and [[2016 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]]. Morris finished the season with 69 carries for 243 yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alfred Morris 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MorrAl00/gamelog/2016/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180302163814/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MorrAl00/gamelog/2016/ |archive-date=March 2, 2018 |access-date=March 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was also declared inactive for the [[2016–17 NFL playoffs#NFC: Green Bay Packers 34, Dallas Cowboys 31|Divisional Round]] loss against the [[2016 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]].

====2017 season====
[[File:Dak Prescott handoff vs Redskins 2017.jpg|thumb|[[Dak Prescott]] hands off the ball to Morris during a game against the Redskins in 2017]]
Morris stayed ahead of McFadden as the backup for [[Ezekiel Elliott]]. He became the starting [[running back]] in Week 10, when Elliott began serving a six-game suspension for violating the [[National Football League player conduct policy|NFL personal conduct policy]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 2, 2017 |title=Cowboys look to Morris to replace Elliott during suspension |url=http://www.foxsports.com/san-diego/story/cowboys-look-to-morris-to-replace-elliott-during-suspension-110217 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190204122334/https://www.foxsports.com/san-diego/story/cowboys-look-to-morris-to-replace-elliott-during-suspension-110217 |archive-date=February 4, 2019 |access-date=February 3, 2019 |website=FOX Sports |language=en-US |agency=Associated Press}}</ref>

On ''[[Thursday Night Football]]'' in Week 13, Morris faced against his former team, the [[2017 Washington Redskins season|Washington Redskins]]. He finished the game with 127 rushing yards, supporting the Cowboys dramatically to a 38–14 win.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Harmon |first=Matt |date=November 30, 2017 |title=Alfred Morris supports Cowboys in big way in aftermath of Elliot's suspension |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/alfred-morris-eases-zeke-elliott-s-absence-for-cowboys-0ap3000000885913 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171202053351/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000885913/article/alfred-morris-eases-zeke-elliotts-absence-for-cowboys |archive-date=December 2, 2017 |access-date=December 1, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

He returned to a backup role in Week 16. During Elliott's absence, he was the team's leading rusher, contributing to the running game and remaining efficient although not dominating, while posting 99 carries for 430 yards (4.3-yard average). Overall, Morris finished the 2017 season with 115 carries for 547 rushing yards (4.8-yard average), a rushing touchdown, and seven receptions for 45 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alfred Morris 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MorrAl00/gamelog/2017/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180302120057/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MorrAl00/gamelog/2017/ |archive-date=March 2, 2018 |access-date=March 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===
On August 13, 2018, Morris signed with the [[San Francisco 49ers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 14, 2018 |title=49ers Sign RB Morris; Waive OL Knott |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-rb-morris-waive-ol-knott |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201002104532/https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-rb-morris-waive-ol-knott |archive-date=October 2, 2020 |access-date=November 13, 2020 |website=49ers.com}}</ref> He was named the starting running back when [[Jerick McKinnon]] went down with a torn ACL. In his first start, he logged 38 yards on 12 carries against the [[2018 Minnesota Vikings season|Minnesota Vikings]] in Week 1.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Minnesota Vikings – September 9th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201809090min.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190107130833/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201809090min.htm |archive-date=January 7, 2019 |access-date=February 3, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the regular season finale against the [[2018 Los Angeles Rams season|Los Angeles Rams]], he had 111 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Los Angeles Rams – December 30th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201812300ram.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200707201022/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201812300ram.htm |archive-date=July 7, 2020 |access-date=February 3, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Overall, he finished the 2018 season with 428 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alfred Morris 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MorrAl00/gamelog/2018/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201115090426/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MorrAl00/gamelog/2018/ |archive-date=November 15, 2020 |access-date=February 3, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys (second stint)===
On July 29, 2019, Morris signed with the Cowboys to ensure experienced veteran depth at the running back position, amid the holdout from [[Ezekiel Elliott]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eatman |first=Nick |date=July 29, 2019 |title=Cowboys To Add Veteran RB Alfred Morris |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/cowboys-to-add-veteran-rb-alfred-morris |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201107231629/https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/cowboys-to-add-veteran-rb-alfred-morris |archive-date=November 7, 2020 |access-date=November 13, 2020 |website=DallasCowboys.com}}</ref> After Elliott received a contract extension, the Cowboys released Morris on September 7.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Helman |first=David |date=September 7, 2019 |title=Zeke Added To Cowboys' 53; Morris Released |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/zeke-added-to-cowboys-53-morris-released |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210227070348/https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/zeke-added-to-cowboys-53-morris-released |archive-date=February 27, 2021 |access-date=November 13, 2020 |website=DallasCowboys.com}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
On October 22, 2019, Morris signed with the [[Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=October 23, 2019 |title=Chase Edmonds Leads Way As Cardinals Sign RBs Alfred Morris, Zach Zenner |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-sign-alfred-morris-zach-zenner-for-rb-depth |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200925162255/https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-sign-alfred-morris-zach-zenner-for-rb-depth |archive-date=September 25, 2020 |access-date=November 13, 2020 |website=AZCardinals.com}}</ref> He was released 10 days later.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Urban |first=Darren |date=November 1, 2019 |title=Cardinals Sign LB Zach Brown, Release RB Alfred Morris |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-sign-lb-zach-brown-release-rb-alfred-morris |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021050547/https://www.azcardinals.com/news/cardinals-sign-lb-zach-brown-release-rb-alfred-morris |archive-date=October 21, 2020 |access-date=November 13, 2020 |website=AZCardinals.com}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On September 29, 2020, the [[New York Giants]] signed Morris to their practice squad, to provide depth after [[Saquon Barkley]] was lost for the season with a torn ACL in his right knee. Morris reunited with [[offensive coordinator]] [[Jason Garrett]], who was his head coach with the Cowboys.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 29, 2020 |title=RB Alfred Morris and QB Clayton Thorson added to practice squad; DB Madre Harper intends to sign Thursday |url=https://www.giants.com/news/madre-harper-alfred-morris-clayton-thorson-practice-squad |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201002102721/https://www.giants.com/news/madre-harper-alfred-morris-clayton-thorson-practice-squad |archive-date=October 2, 2020 |access-date=September 30, 2020 |website=Giants.com}}</ref>

Morris was elevated to the active roster on November 2, 2020, for the team's Week 8 game against the [[2020 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 2, 2020 |title=Giants' Alfred Morris: Promoted to active roster |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/giants-alfred-morris-promoted-to-active-roster/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221004011729/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/giants-alfred-morris-promoted-to-active-roster/ |archive-date=October 4, 2022 |access-date=November 10, 2020 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> He was reverted to the practice squad following the game<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 3, 2020 |title=Alfred Morris: Goes back to practice squad |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/alfred-morris-goes-back-to-practice-squad/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221004011730/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/alfred-morris-goes-back-to-practice-squad/ |archive-date=October 4, 2022 |access-date=November 10, 2020 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> and was elevated again on November 7 for the Week 9 game against the [[2020 Washington Football Team season|Washington Football Team]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 7, 2020 |title=Giants' Alfred Morris: Back on active roster |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/giants-alfred-morris-back-on-active-roster/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221004011731/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/giants-alfred-morris-back-on-active-roster/ |archive-date=October 4, 2022 |access-date=November 10, 2020 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> Morris reverted to the practice squad again following the game, and he was promoted to the active roster on November 13.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=November 13, 2020 |title=Giants place Devonta Freeman on IR; Alfred Morris, Montre Hartage signed off practice squad |url=https://www.giants.com/news/giants-place-devonta-freeman-on-ir-alfred-morris-montre-hartage-signed-off-pract |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210126125837/https://www.giants.com/news/giants-place-devonta-freeman-on-ir-alfred-morris-montre-hartage-signed-off-pract |archive-date=January 26, 2021 |access-date=October 3, 2022 |website=Giants.com}}</ref>

Morris spent most of the season with [[Dion Lewis]] as backups to [[Wayne Gallman]]. He finished the season playing in nine games, rushing 55 times for 238 yards and a touchdown along with three receptions for 19 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alfred Morris 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MorrAl00/gamelog/2020/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202200322/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MorrAl00/gamelog/2020/ |archive-date=December 2, 2021 |access-date=October 4, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Morris re-signed with the Giants on August 2, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=August 2, 2021 |title=Giants re-sign veteran running back Alfred Morris |url=https://www.giants.com/news/alfred-morris-signs-giants-saquon-barkley-running-back |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210802162330/https://www.giants.com/news/alfred-morris-signs-giants-saquon-barkley-running-back |archive-date=August 2, 2021 |access-date=October 3, 2022 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> He was released on August 16, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=August 17, 2021 |title=Giants make 3 transactions to reach NFL's 85-player roster limit |url=https://www.giants.com/news/alfred-morris-chris-milton-jarren-williams-roster-transaction-2021-nfl-season |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210817141746/https://www.giants.com/news/alfred-morris-chris-milton-jarren-williams-roster-transaction-2021-nfl-season |archive-date=August 17, 2021 |access-date=October 3, 2022 |website=Giants.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Morris is the son of Ronald and Yvonne Morris. He has six brothers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jones |first=Mike |date=September 4, 2012 |title=Redskins RB Alfred Morris: Parents' example is key to his success |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2012/09/04/redskins-rb-alfred-morris-parents-example-is-key-to-his-success/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130724160117/http://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2012/09/04/redskins-rb-alfred-morris-parents-example-is-key-to-his-success/ |archive-date=July 24, 2013 |access-date=September 4, 2012 |website=WashingtonPost.com}}</ref> Morris is a [[Christianity|Christian]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alfred Morris |url=http://www.fca.org/magazine/2013/08/29/alfred-morris-washington-redskins |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924010944/http://www.fca.org/magazine/2013/08/29/alfred-morris-washington-redskins |archive-date=September 24, 2015 |access-date=August 4, 2015 |website=FCA.org}}</ref>

Despite being able to afford a new car, he still drives his 1991 [[Mazda Capella|Mazda 626]], which he nicknamed "Bentley".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walker |first=Andrew |date=September 19, 2012 |title=Alfred Morris Won't Give Up His 'Bentley' |url=http://blog.redskins.com/2012/09/19/alfred-morris-wont-give-up-his-bentley/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120924054305/http://blog.redskins.com/2012/09/19/alfred-morris-wont-give-up-his-bentley/ |archive-date=September 24, 2012 |access-date=September 30, 2012 |website=Redskins.com}}</ref> He drove this car from [[Boca Raton, Florida]], to his new D.C. home. Due to the positive publicity, [[Mazda]] refurbished the car free of charge. As part of the refurbishment, the car received a new radio featuring a [[CD player]] and a [[Automotive navigation system|navigation system]] but otherwise was restored to factory floor condition.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brinson |first=Will |date=July 25, 2013 |title=Mazda is refurbishing Alfred Morris' infamous 1991 'Bentley' |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/mazda-is-refurbishing-alfred-morris-infamous-1991-bentley/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201114115758/https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/mazda-is-refurbishing-alfred-morris-infamous-1991-bentley/ |archive-date=November 14, 2020 |access-date=November 13, 2020 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> Mazda later launched a similar program in 2017 for Japanese owners of the first generation [[Mazda MX-5]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Woodard |first=Collin |date=August 4, 2017 |title=Mazda Will Make Old NA Miatas Brand New Again |url=http://www.motortrend.com/news/mazda-will-make-na-miata-brand-new/?sm_id=organic_fb_social_MT_170804_sf103808368#sf103808368 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190413025745/https://www.motortrend.com/news/mazda-will-make-na-miata-brand-new/?sm_id=organic_fb_social_MT_170804_sf103808368#sf103808368 |archive-date=April 13, 2019 |access-date=November 13, 2020 |website=Motortrend.com}}</ref>

'''Allama Uzair Matthews''' (born August 24, 1961) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] and [[h-back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).

Born and raised in [[Jacksonville, Florida]], Matthews played scholastically at [[Andrew Jackson High School (Jacksonville)|Andrew Jackson High School]].<ref name="PFR1">{{cite web| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MattAl00.htm |title=Allama Matthews Stats |website=Pro Football Reference |access-date=June 2, 2024}}</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt Commodores]],<ref name="NFL">{{cite web| url=https://www.nfl.com/players/allama-matthews/ |title=Allama Matthews Stats |website=NFL.com |access-date=June 2, 2024}}</ref> where, as a senior, he was honored by ''[[The Football News]]'' as a first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]].<ref name="FN 1982">{{cite news |title=Football News All-America Team |newspaper=The Gazette (Cedar Rapids (IA) |date=November 19, 1982 |page=2C |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-gazette-1982-football-news-all-ameri/147793176/ |access-date=June 2, 2024 |via=Newspapers.com}} {{Open access}}</ref>

Early in his [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt]] career, coaches tried Matthews at safety and receiver. Once all parties settled on tight end, Matthews put together one of the finest receiving campaigns ever, helping spark the team's run to the [[1982 Hall of Fame Classic|Hall of Fame Bowl]]. In 1982, Matthews was named first-team All-America by Football News after posting 61 receptions for 797 yards and 14 TDs, most ever by a Commodore. Later that season, Matthews was also named SEC Offensive Lineman of the Year by the Atlanta Touchdown Club. Matthews also earned [[1982 All-SEC football team|First-team All-SEC]] honors by the Associated Press and United Press International in 1982. He concluded his Vanderbilt career with 18 touchdowns.<ref>[https://vucommodores.com/allama-matthews]/</ref>

Matthews was selected by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] in the twelfth-round of the [[1983 NFL draft]].<ref name="PFR2">{{Cite web |title=1983 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1983/draft.htm |access-date=June 2, 2024 |website=Pro Football Reference}}</ref> He spent three seasons with the Falcons, appearing in 37 games, with 11 receptions and 1 touchdown.<ref name="PFA">{{Cite web |url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/playerm/matt01400.html |title=Allama Matthews Stats |website=Pro Football Archives |access-date=June 2, 2024 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230423102906/https://www.profootballarchives.com/playerm/matt01400.html |archive-date=April 23, 2023}}</ref>

'''Alfred Calvin Blue III''' (born April 27, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Houston Texans]] in the sixth round of the [[2014 NFL draft]]. Blue is from [[Boutte, Louisiana]] and attended [[Hahnville High School]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[LSU Tigers football|LSU Tigers]].

Blue remained with the Texans for five seasons, primarily as a reserve player. He received his greatest amount of playing time in 2015, when he started 9 out of 16 games. In 2019, he signed with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], but was released without playing a single game.

==Early life==
Blue attended and played [[high school football]] at [[Hahnville High School]]. He rushed for 1,695 yards and 25 touchdowns along with 13 receptions for nearly 200 yards and three touchdowns in his senior season in 2009. Blue was a member of the SuperPrep Southwest Team and was named to the Baton Rouge Advocate Super Dozen. Blue earned the honors of the Class 5A all-state first-team in 2009 and was selected as the District 6-5A 2009 Offensive MVP. Blue was also on the school's [[track and field|track]] team, where he ran the 200-meter dash in 23.5 and the 4 × 200 m relay in 1:28.70. Blue was ranked as a three-star prospect by ''[[Rivals.com|Rivals]]'' and ''[[Scout.com]]''. Blue committed to [[LSU football|LSU]] to play college football under [[Les Miles]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ganguli |first=Tania |date=September 25, 2014 |title=Football has always helped Alfred Blue cope with tragedy and pain |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/houston-texans/post/_/id/7688/football-helped-blue-cope-with-family-pain |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401215148/http://www.espn.com/blog/houston-texans/post/_/id/7688/football-helped-blue-cope-with-family-pain |archive-date=April 1, 2019 |access-date=March 6, 2018 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Alfred Blue, 2010 Running Back |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2010/alfred-blue-23212 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221005014817/https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2010/alfred-blue-23212 |archive-date=October 5, 2022 |access-date=October 16, 2022 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Alfred Blue, Houston Texans, Running Back |url=https://247sports.com/player/alfred-blue-2624/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170816170107/http://247sports.com/player/alfred-blue-2624 |archive-date=August 16, 2017 |access-date=October 16, 2022 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Alexander''' "'''Ali'''" '''Marpet''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|æ|l|i|_|m|ɑr|ˈ|p|ɛ|t}}; born April 17, 1993) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (American football)|guard]] for seven seasons with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).

Marpet played [[college football]] for the [[Hobart Statesmen football|Hobart Statesmen]], an [[NCAA Division III]] program. In 2014, he was a ''[[Lindy's Sports|Lindy's]]'' preseason [[All-American]] first-team, [[American Football Coaches Association]] (AFCA) All-American, D3football.com All-America first-team, and [[Liberty League]] Co-Offensive Player of the Year.

He attended the [[2015 Senior Bowl]], as the first [[NCAA Division III]] player picked to play in the all-star game in 25 years. ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' named Marpet the "biggest riser" at the game, and included him on its All-Offense team. At the [[Scouting Combine]] in February 2015, he ran the fastest [[40-yard dash]] among [[offensive line]] prospects eligible for the 2015 NFL Draft (4.98), the fastest {{convert|10|yd|m|adj=on}} split (1.74 seconds), and also the second-best time in the [[three-cone drill]] (7.33) and [[20-yard shuttle]] (4.47), while scoring the highest "Speed, Power, Agility, Reaction and Quickness" ([[SPARQ Training|SPARQ]]) score. He also performed 30 repetitions at {{convert|225|lb|kg}} in the [[bench press]], tied for fifth-best among offensive linemen. He also had a vertical leap of greater than 30 inches, and a [[Wonderlic test]] intelligence score of over 30.

Drafted in the second round, 61st overall, of the [[2015 NFL draft]] by the Buccaneers, Marpet is the highest-drafted pick in the history of Division III football.<ref name="nbcsports.com">{{Cite web |last=McGuire |first=Kevin |date=May 2, 2015 |title=Ali Marpet puts D3 Hobart on the NFL Draft scoreboard – College Football Talk |url=http://collegefootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/05/02/ali-marpet-puts-d3-hobart-on-the-nfl-draft-scoreboard/ |access-date=February 10, 2023 |website=NBC Sports |archive-date=May 24, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150524102547/http://collegefootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2015/05/02/ali-marpet-puts-d3-hobart-on-the-nfl-draft-scoreboard/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2015–2017===

===Retirement===
On February 27, 2022, Marpet announced his retirement from professional football at age 28 after seven seasons via an Instagram post.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maya |first=Adam |date=February 27, 2022 |title=Buccaneers' Pro Bowl guard Ali Marpet announces retirement after seven seasons |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/buccaneers-pro-bowl-guard-ali-marpet-announces-retirement-after-seven-seasons |access-date=February 10, 2023 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US |archive-date=February 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230210213420/https://www.nfl.com/news/buccaneers-pro-bowl-guard-ali-marpet-announces-retirement-after-seven-seasons |url-status=live }}</ref> He retired with two years left on his contract, with an annual salary of $10 million. Many former teammates, including [[Tom Brady]], wished Marpet congratulations on his retirement via various social media platforms.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Laine |first=Jenna |date=February 27, 2022 |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers Pro Bowl guard Ali Marpet retires at age 28 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/33386571/tampa-bay-buccaneers-pro-bowl-guard-ali-marpet-retires-age-28 |access-date=February 27, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |archive-date=February 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220227204946/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/33386571/tampa-bay-buccaneers-pro-bowl-guard-ali-marpet-retires-age-28 |url-status=live }}</ref>

'''Alexander Mattison''' (born June 19, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Boise State Broncos football|Boise State Broncos]] and was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the third round of the [[2019 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Mattison attended [[San Bernardino High School]] in [[San Bernardino, California]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-07-02 |title=Raiders’ running back gets high school jersey retired in San Bernardino |url=https://www.kvcrnews.org/local-news/2024-07-02/raiders-running-back-gets-high-school-jersey-retired-in-san-bernardino |access-date=2025-03-25 |website=KVCR News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Ho |first=Matthew |date=2024-06-28 |title=How NFL running back Alexander Mattison’s mental health journey led to his youth football camp |url=https://www.sbsun.com/2024/06/28/how-nfl-running-back-alexander-mattisons-mental-health-journey-led-to-his-youth-football-camp/ |access-date=2025-03-25 |website=San Bernardino Sun |language=en-US}}</ref> where he played [[high school football]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marshall |first=Pete |date=September 17, 2015 |title=Alexander Mattison hoping to show you can succeed coming from San Bernardino High |url=http://www.dailybulletin.com/sports/20150917/alexander-mattison-hoping-to-show-you-can-succeed-coming-from-san-bernardino-high |access-date=September 20, 2019 |website=Daily Bulletin}}</ref> He rushed for over 2,000 yards in each of his final two seasons, going for 2,017 yards and 26 [[touchdowns]] as a junior and 2,057 yards and 22 touchdowns as a senior.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Southorn |first=Dave |date=November 10, 2016 |title=Boise State freshman running back Alexander Mattison mature beyond his years |url=https://www.idahostatesman.com/sports/college/mountain-west/boise-state-university/boise-state-football/article113848033.html |access-date=September 20, 2019 |website=Idaho Statesman}}</ref> Mattison was selected to play in the Inland Valley Football Classic following his senior season. In addition to football, Mattison also ran track and wrestled. As a senior, he won the [[Mountain Valley League]] title in the [[110 metres hurdles|110m hurdles]]. His personal-bests are 14.95 seconds (110m hurdles), 11.34s ([[100 metres|100 meters]]), 23.34s ([[200 metres|200 meters]]), {{convert|22|ft|9|in|m|abbr=on}} in the [[long jump]] and {{convert|46|ft|5.5|in|m|abbr=on}} in the [[shot put]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alexander Mattison |url=https://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/Athlete.aspx?AID=5393382 |url-status=dead |website=Athletic.net |access-date=November 15, 2019 |archive-date=May 30, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160530162938/http://www.athletic.net/TrackAndField/Athlete.aspx?AID=5393382 }}</ref> He also won a league wrestling title at 195 pounds and was named all-league as a junior. He committed to [[Boise State University]] to play [[college football]].

==College career==
As a [[Glossary of American football terms#T|true freshman]] at Boise State in 2016, Mattison appeared in all 13 games and had 328 yards on 67 carries with four touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Southorn |first=Dave |date=July 14, 2017 |title=Alexander Mattison poised for starring role in Boise State offense |url=https://magicvalley.com/sports/college/bsu/alexander-mattison-poised-for-starring-role-in-boise-state-offense/article_4b9c1ff1-96d3-58bc-99d9-cbd8a76724bf.html |access-date=September 20, 2019 |website=Twin Falls Times-News}}</ref> As a sophomore, he played in all 14 games, rushing for 1,086 yards on 212 carries and 12 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wustrow |first=John |date=November 9, 2018 |title=Mattison continues late push for another 1,000-yard season with big game against Fresno State |url=https://www.idahopress.com/blueturfsports/football/mattison-continues-late-push-for-another--yard-season-with/article_7ab81fc6-eaad-5689-a1a7-15ec8db1917d.html |access-date=September 20, 2019 |website=Idaho Press}}</ref>

As a junior in 2018, he rushed for 1,415 yards on 302 carries with 17 touchdowns in 13 games. He was the Offensive MVP of the [[2018 Mountain West Conference Football Championship Game]] after rushing for 200 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wustrow |first=John |date=December 1, 2018 |title=Mattison's late heroics not enough to lift Boise State again |url=https://www.idahopress.com/blueturfsports/football/mattison-s-late-heroics-not-enough-to-lift-boise-state/article_19805f1b-4a27-5119-b7ec-249506f2c3c8.html |access-date=September 20, 2019 |website=Idaho Press}}</ref>

After the season, Mattison entered the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crippe |first=Chad |date=December 28, 2018 |title=Boise State's star running back enters NFL Draft, extends recent trend |url=https://www.idahostatesman.com/sports/college/mountain-west/boise-state-university/boise-state-football/article223701390.html |access-date=September 20, 2019 |website=Idaho Statesman}}</ref> He cited his reason as "You can only play as long as your body lets you, and at this position, you can't assume it'll last forever." Mattison didn't miss a game in his college career, despite needing offseason surgeries on his shoulder and ankle.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Southorn |first=Dave |date=December 31, 2018 |title=Why go? Boise State's Alexander Mattison explains his decision to leave for NFL |url=https://www.idahostatesman.com/sports/college/mountain-west/boise-state-university/boise-state-football/article223756120.html |access-date=September 20, 2019 |website=Idaho Statesman}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
The [[Minnesota Vikings]] selected Mattison in the third round (102nd overall) of the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Craig |date=April 26, 2019 |title=Vikings Draft Boise State RB Alexander Mattison in 3rd Round of NFL Draft |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-draft-boise-state-rb-alexander-mattison-in-3rd-round-of-nfl-draft |access-date=September 20, 2019 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref> He made his NFL debut in the 2019 regular season opener against the [[Atlanta Falcons]]; Mattison had nine carries for 49 yards in the 28–12 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 9, 2019 |title=Vikings Snap Counts: Rookie Mattison makes most of limited playing time |url=http://www.foxsports.com/north/story/minnesota-vikings-snap-counts-week-1-atlanta-falcons-alexander-mattison-090919 |access-date=September 20, 2019 |website=FOX Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> In Week 3 against the [[Oakland Raiders]], Mattison rushed 12 times for 58 yards and his first career rushing touchdown as the Vikings won 34–14.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 22, 2019 |title=NFL rushing leader Cook leads Vikes romp past Raiders 34–14 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127956 |access-date=September 22, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Overall, he finished his rookie season with 462 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alexander Mattison 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MattAl01/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=January 7, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In a Week 5 ''[[NBC Sunday Night Football|Sunday Night Football]]'' game against the [[Seattle Seahawks]], Mattison finished with 20 carries for 112 rushing yards as the Vikings narrowly lost 26–27. Fellow teammate and running back [[Dalvin Cook]] was injured in the game, allowing Mattison to record his first game with at least 100 rushing yards as a professional.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Seattle Seahawks – October 11th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202010110sea.htm |access-date=October 11, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Schad |first=Chris |date=October 11, 2020 |title=Late score drops Vikings in Seattle |url=https://bringmethenews.com/minnesota-sports/late-score-drops-vikings-in-seattle |access-date=September 21, 2023 |website=Bring Me The News |language=en}}</ref> In the 2020 season, Mattison had 96 carries for 434 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns, to go along with 13 receptions for 125 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown, in 13 games with two starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alexander Mattison 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MattAl01/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=September 21, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In the 2021 season, Mattison appeared in 16 games with four starts. He had 134 carries for 491 rushing yards and three rushing touchdowns, to go along with 32 receptions for 228 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alexander Mattison 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MattAl01/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=September 21, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In the 2022 season, Mattison appeared in all 17 games. He finished with 74 carries for 283 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns, as well as 15 receptions for 91 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alexander Mattison 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MattAl01/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=September 21, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On March 17, 2023, Mattison signed a two-year, $7 million contract extension with the Vikings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Young |first=Lindsey |date=March 16, 2023 |title=Vikings Agree to Terms with Alexander Mattison to Keep RB in Purple |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/alexander-mattison-running-back-free-agency |access-date=September 21, 2023 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref> With the departure of Cook in the offseason, Mattison earned the opportunity to start for the Vikings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Michael David |date=July 6, 2023 |title=Alexander Mattison sees "great opportunity" in being Vikings' starting running back |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/alexander-mattison-sees-great-opportunity-in-being-vikings-starting-running-back |access-date=September 21, 2023 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> In 16 games with 13 starts, he recorded 180 carries for 700 rushing yards, as well as 30 receptions for 192 receiving yards and three receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alexander Mattison 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MattAl01.htm |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He committed three fumbles, recovering one.

On March 4, 2024, Mattison was released by the Vikings after five seasons.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peters |first=Craig |date=March 4, 2024 |title=Vikings Release Running Back Alexander Mattison |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/alexander-mattison-release-running-back-2024 |access-date=4 March 2024 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
On March 18, 2024, Mattison signed with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 18, 2024 |title=Raiders sign RB Alexander Mattison |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-alexander-mattison-running-back-nfl-2024-free-agency-transactions |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=Raiders.com}}</ref>

In Week 9, Mattison had 123 all-purpose yards, 92 yards on 23 carries and 31 yards on three receptions, in the 20–15 loss against the [[Los Angeles Rams]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 20, 2024 |title=Rams 20-15 Raiders (Oct 20, 2024) Final Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/game/_/gameId/401671663/raiders-rams |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=ESPN}}</ref> In Week 11, Mattison suffered an ankle injury in the 34–19 loss against the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref name="j492">{{cite web | title=Raiders' Alexander Mattison: Injures ankle Sunday | website=CBSSports.com | date=2024-11-17 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/raiders-alexander-mattison-injures-ankle-sunday/ | access-date=2024-12-26}}</ref> He missed Week 12's matchup against [[Denver Broncos]] and Week 13's matchup against [[Kansas City Chiefs]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Straub |first=Luke |date=November 24, 2024 |title=Raiders winners and losers in 29-19 defeat vs. Broncos |url=https://raiderswire.usatoday.com/2024/11/24/raiders-winners-and-losers-in-29-19-defeat-vs-broncos/ |access-date=March 26, 2026 |website=Raiders Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Skrive |first=Data |date=November 29, 2024 |title=Raiders down top 2 running backs again Week 13 vs Chiefs |url=https://raiderswire.usatoday.com/2024/11/29/raiders-running-backs-zamir-white-alexander-mattison-inactives-week-13-chiefs/ |access-date=March 26, 2026 |website=Raiders Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> In the 2024 season, Mattison had 132 carries for 420 rushing yards and four rushing touchdowns to go with 36 receptions for 294 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alexander Mattison 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MattAl01/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2025-02-24 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
On March 14, 2025, Mattison signed a one-year contract with the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/44239590/source-dolphins-reach-1-year-deal-rb-alexander-mattison|work=ESPN.com|title=Source: Dolphins reach 1-year deal with RB Alexander Mattison|first=Marcel|last=Louis-Jacques|date=March 13, 2025|accessdate=March 17, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.miamidolphins.com/news/dolphins-sign-mattison|work=MiamiDolphins.com|title=Dolphins Sign Mattison|date=March 14, 2025|accessdate=March 17, 2025}}</ref> On August 10, Mattison hurt his neck during a preseason game against the [[Chicago Bears]] and had to be taken to a hospital for season-ending surgery.<ref>{{cite web | last=Smith | first=Michael David | title=Dolphins lose running back Alexander Mattison for season with neck injury | website=NBC Sports | date=2025-08-11 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/dolphins-lose-running-back-alexander-mattison-for-season-with-neck-injury | access-date=2026-03-19}}</ref>

'''Alexander Hollins''' (born November 24, 1996) is an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[wide receiver]] for the [[Montreal Alouettes]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He played college football for [[Eastern Illinois Panthers football|Eastern Illinois]]. Hollins has played for the [[Minnesota Vikings]], [[Cleveland Browns]], and [[BC Lions]].

==Early life==
Hollins grew up in [[Yazoo City, Mississippi]], and attended [[Yazoo County High School]]. As a senior, he had 64 receptions for 1,346 yards and 15 touchdowns.<ref name="Hollins reflects"/>

==College career==
Hollins began his collegiate career at [[Copiah–Lincoln Community College]]. He caught 11 passes for 214 yards and three touchdowns as a sophomore before transferring to [[Eastern Illinois University]] for the final two years of his NCAA eligibility.<ref name="Hollins reflects">{{cite web|url=https://www.dailyeasternnews.com/2018/09/19/hollins-reflects-on-career-game-future-in-football/|title=Hollins reflects on career game, future in football|first=JJ|last=Bullock|work=[[The Daily Eastern News]]|date=September 19, 2018|access-date=December 2, 2019}}</ref>

In his first season with the [[Eastern Illinois Panthers football|Panthers]], Hollins led the team with 47 receptions for 694 yards and seven touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://herald-review.com/sports/college/eiu-football-ready-to-show-off-new-offense/article_7fe30db2-f215-534e-ae86-6cd2f797bedc.html|title=EIU football ready to show off new offense|first=Sandy|last=King|work=[[Herald & Review]]|date=July 23, 2019|access-date=December 2, 2019}}</ref> As a senior, he caught 80 passes for 1,102 yards and 16 touchdowns and was named first-team All-[[Ohio Valley Conference]]. Hollins had 127 receptions, 1,796 yards and 23 touchdowns in 22 games at Eastern Illinois.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://jg-tc.com/sports/former-eastern-illinois-wide-receiver-alexander-hollins-signs-with-minnesota/article_de63535b-6ce2-5e95-8282-0020341dd882.html|title=Former Eastern Illinois wide receiver Alexander Hollins signs with Minnesota Vikings as undrafted free agent|first=Patrick|last=Engel|work=Journal Gazette|date=April 27, 2019|access-date=December 2, 2019}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
Hollins signed with the [[Minnesota Vikings]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] on April 29, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/vikings-agree-to-terms-with-undrafted-free-agents|title=Vikings Agree to Terms with Undrafted Free Agents|first=Craig|last=Peters|website=Vikings.com|date=April 29, 2019|access-date=December 2, 2019}}</ref> He was waived by the team at the end of training camp during final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/alexander-hollins-exits-minnesota/|title=Alexander Hollins: Exits Minnesota|website=[[CBSSports.com]]|publisher=[[RotoWire]]|date=August 30, 2019|access-date=December 2, 2019}}</ref> Hollins was re-signed by the Vikings to their practice squad on September 12, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dailynorseman.com/2019/9/12/20863600/minnesota-vikings-nate-meadors-active-roster-alexander-hollins-practice-squad|title=Vikings elevate Nate Meadors to active roster, sign Alexander Hollins to practice squad|first=Christopher|last=Gates|website=DailyNorseman.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=September 12, 2019|access-date=December 2, 2019}}</ref> Hollins was promoted to the Vikings active roster on December 2, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://vikingswire.usatoday.com/2019/12/02/vikings-place-lb-ben-gedeon-on-ir-sign-wr-alexander-hollins/|title=Vikings place LB Ben Gedeon on IR, sign WR Alexander Hollins|first=Kyle|last=Ratke|website=Vikings Wire|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=December 2, 2019|access-date=December 2, 2019}}</ref> Hollins played in four games as a rookie and caught two passes for 46 yards in the Vikings' final regular season game against the [[Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/kirk-cousins-2020-season-embracing-continuity-turnover|title=Kirk Cousins Embracing Continuity & Turnover of 2020 Vikings|first=Lindsey|last=Young|website=Vikings.com|date=August 7, 2020|access-date=August 26, 2020}}</ref>

Hollins was waived by the Vikings on September 5, 2020, and signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Peters |first1=Craig |last2=Smith |first2=Eric |title=Vikings Announce Roster Moves, Set Initial 53-Man Roster |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/2020-roster-53-man-announced |website=Minnesota Vikings |access-date=September 5, 2020 |date=September 5, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Vikings Claim LB Ryan Connelly, Add 13 Players To Practice Squad|url=https://www.vikings.com/news/ryan-connelly-2020-practice-squad-add-13-players|website=Vikings.com|date=September 6, 2020}}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
Hollins was signed off the Vikings' practice squad to the [[Cleveland Browns]]' active roster on December 28, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Browns sign WR Alexander Hollins |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-sign-wr-alexander-hollins |publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=December 28, 2020}}</ref> The Browns waived Hollins on August 23, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Browns place K Cody Parkey on injured reserve, reduce roster to 80 |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-place-k-cody-parkey-on-injured-reserve-reduce-roster-to-80 |publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=August 23, 2021 |access-date=August 23, 2021 |archive-date=December 19, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221219144559/https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-place-k-cody-parkey-on-injured-reserve-reduce-roster-to-80 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was re-signed to the practice squad on December 15, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Browns place 6 on reserve/COVID lists, make additional roster moves|url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-place-6-on-reserve-covid-lists-make-additional-roster-moves|website=ClevelandBrowns.com|date=December 15, 2021}}</ref> The Browns waived Hollins off their practice squad on December 21, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Browns place DE Takkarist McKinley on injured reserve, sign DE Porter Gustin to active roster |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-place-de-takkarist-mckinley-on-injured-reserve-sign-de-porter-gustin-to-a |publisher=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=December 21, 2021}}</ref>

=== BC Lions ===
Hollins signed with the [[BC Lions]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) on March 1, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |agency=The Canadian Press |date=2022-03-01 |title=Lions add RB Anderson III, WR Hollins - TSN.ca |url=https://www.tsn.ca/bc-lions-bruce-anderson-iii-alexander-hollins-1.1765148 |access-date=2022-03-07 |website=TSN |language=en}}</ref> He made his CFL debut on October 8, 2022, where he had three catches for 47 yards and one touchdown against the [[Toronto Argonauts]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/games/6277/bc-lions-vs-toronto-argonauts/ |title=Game Notes |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |date=October 8, 2022}}</ref> He played and started in four regular season games where he had 13 receptions for 117 yards and one touchdown.<ref name=CFLguide>{{cite web|url=https://static.cfl.ca/wp-content/uploads/2050/11/2024-CFL-Guide-Digital.pdf |title=2024 CFL Guide |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=June 22, 2024}}</ref> He made his post-season debut in the West Semi-Final victory over the [[Calgary Stampeders]] and played in playoff games, recording eight catches for 102 yards and a touchdown.<ref name=CFLguide/>

In [[2023 BC Lions season|2023]], Hollins won a starting role in training camp and had a breakout season.<ref name=CFLguide/> He played and started in all 18 regular season games where he had 78 catches for 1,173 yards and nine touchdowns.<ref name=CFLguide/> At season's end, he was named a CFL West All-Star.<ref name="divstars">{{cite web|title=In the Stars: 2023 Division All-Stars unveiled |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2023/11/02/in-the-stars-2023-division-all-stars-unveiled/ |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] | date=November 2, 2023}}</ref>

In the first six games of the [[2024 BC Lions season|2024 season]], Hollins had 38 receptions for 656 yards and four touchdowns.<ref name=CFLbio>{{cite web|title=Alexander Hollins |url=https://www.cfl.ca/players/alexander-hollins/165196/ |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=February 1, 2025}}</ref> However, following an injury and demotion of quarterback [[Vernon Adams]], Hollins struggled to maintain his outstanding production and finished the season with 61 catches for 937 yards and six touchdowns in 16 games played.<ref name=CFLbio/> In the West Semi-Final, he had two receptions for 16 yards.<ref name=BCrelease/> With one year remaining on his contract, he was released on January 30, 2025.<ref name=BCrelease>{{cite web|title=Report: Lions release receiver Alexander Hollins |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2025/01/30/report-lions-to-release-receiver-alexander-hollins/ |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |date=January 30, 2025}}</ref>

===Edmonton Elks===
On April 28, 2025, it was announced that Hollins had signed with the [[Edmonton Elks]].<ref name=EDMsigned>{{cite web|title=TRANSACTIONS: Elks sign dynamic wideout Alexander Hollins |url=https://www.goelks.com/2025/04/28/transactions-elks-sign-dynamic-wideout-alexander-hollins/ |publisher=[[Edmonton Elks]] |date=April 28, 2025}}</ref> However, he was released on June 1, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|title=Transactions – Football Player Trades and Signings |url=https://www.cfl.ca/transactions/2025/ |publisher=[[Canadian Football League]] |access-date=June 5, 2025}}</ref>

===Montreal Alouettes===
On July 1, 2025, it was announced that Hollins had signed with the [[Montreal Alouettes]].<ref name=MTLsigned>{{cite web|title=Als sign Americans Alexander Hollins and Caleb Johnson |url=https://en.montrealalouettes.com/2025/07/01/als-sign-americans-alexander-hollins-and-caleb-johnson/ |publisher=[[Montreal Alouettes]] |date=July 1, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.montrealgazette.com/sports/football/montreal-alouettes/article1024472.html | title=New Alouettes receiver Alexander Hollins beat the CFL at its own game | work=[[The Gazette (Montreal)|The Gazette]] | date=July 3, 2025 | accessdate=22 August 2025 | author=Zurkowsky, Herb}}</ref> On January 5th, 2026 Hollins signed a one year extension with the Alouettes.

'''Alijah Holder''' (born January 26, 1996) is an American former [[American football|football]] [[safety (gridiron football position)|safety]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford]].

==College career==
Holder played as a cornerback for the Stanford Cardinals. He did not play during his freshman year in 2014. Holder's first active season was played during his sophomore year in 2015; before he missed nine games due to injury during his junior year in 2016. After recovery, Holder played only four games during his junior year. During his senior year in 2017, Holder was named part of the Pac-12 All-Academic second-team. He played a fifth season in 2018, starting 10 of 12 games. Holder earned honorable mention in the 2018 All-Pac-12. He also became a three-time Pac-12 All-Academic. While at Stanford, Holder majored in [[Media Studies|media studies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gostanford.com/sports/football/roster/alijah-holder/13993|title=Alijah Holder Stanford football Profile|accessdate=May 7, 2022}}</ref>

'''Alexander Myres''' (born April 20, 1996) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] program [[Ouachita Baptist Tigers football|Ouachita Baptist Tigers]] before transferring to the [[Houston Cougars football|Houston Cougars]] of the [[NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision]] (FBS).

He was signed by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] as an undrafted free agent in 2019, seeing no game action during his rookie year. He was then signed by the [[Detroit Lions]], with whom he played in his only NFL game in 2020. He then spent the next two offseasons with the [[San Francisco 49ers]] and the [[Indianapolis Colts]], respectively.

In 2023, he played for the [[Houston Roughnecks (2020)|Houston Roughnecks]] of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]].

==Early life==
Myres attended [[The Woodlands College Park High School|College Park High School]] in [[The Woodlands, Texas]]. As a three-year letterer, Myers made 109 total tackles, 3 forced fumbles, 2 interceptions, and a defensive touchdown made after forcing a fumble on a punt return.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alexander Myres bio|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/alexander-myres/GbHN8_7JEeKZ5AAmVebBJg/default.htm|work=Max Preps}}</ref> He earned All-District First-team and All-County Second-team selection titles as a junior and senior on a state-ranked defense, and he was also selected to participate in the All-Star [[Bayou Bowl]]. Outside of football, Myres also lettered in basketball and track. He currently holds his school's all-time record in the 100M dash and advanced to Texas 6A quarterfinals as a senior.<ref>{{cite web|title=Conroe Woodlands College Park HS Outdoor Team Records|url=https://www.athletic.net/trackandfield/SchoolRecords.aspx?SchoolID=4187|website=Athletic.Net}}</ref>

Despite his performance, Alex Myres was lightly recruited out of high school. According to 247sports and Rivals.com, Myres was listed as a zero-star recruit, and he was the only starting defensive back on his team to not receive a D1 scholarship.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alexander Myres HS Football recruiting profile |url=https://247sports.com/player/alexander-myres-46098164/}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Stephan Johnson, Texas State |url=https://txstatebobcats.com/sports/football/roster/stephan-johnson/5921}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ryder Lucas, Arkansas Football |date=8 May 2015 |url=https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/roster/ryder-lucas/}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Tristen Newman, Stanford |url=https://gostanford.com/sports/track-and-field/roster/tristen-newman/12680}}</ref> Myres's only D1 offers came as preferred walk-on's from [[Towson University]] and [[UTEP]], but both were too expensive and he instead accepted a full-ride to [[Ouachita Baptist]], a Division 2 program.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ouachita Tigers bio|url=https://obutigers.com/sports/football/roster/alex-myres/1848|website=OBUTigers.com}}</ref>

==College career==
During his true freshman season at Ouachita Baptist, Myres made only one start at cornerback but appeared in all games on special teams, making 15 tackles. However, he broke out with a stellar sophomore season, making 79 tackles, 7 sacks, 2 forced fumbles, and 1 interception returned for 57 yards. He had the 10th most tackles among all Division 2 defensive backs from the 2015 season, broke all-time school records, and was named a 2015 D2 All-American.<ref>{{cite web |title=Beating The Odds: From D2 Zero to D1 Hero |date=7 July 2020 |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/texans/article/Steelers-corner-UH-alum-Alex-Myres-beating-the-15389827.php |publisher=Houston Chronicle}}</ref> He then transferred to [[University of Houston]].

After redshirting his first year at UH due to NCAA transfer rules, Myres finished his junior season with 47 tackles, 1 recovered fumble for a touchdown, and 1 interception for 13 yards on 9 starts and 11 game appearances. He was awarded player of the game in the [[Hawaii Bowl]] against [[Fresno State]] when he scooped up a blocked field goal and returned it for a 97-yard touchdown. As a senior, he started in all games and made 65 tackles and 2 interceptions. Entering the NFL draft, Myers had completed his career at Houston with 112 tackles, and his total career with over 200 tackles.

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
After going undrafted in the [[2019 NFL draft]], Myres was signed by the Steelers as an [[undrafted free agent]] for training camp on April 27, 2019.  On July 31, 2019, he was cut following a non-injury related illness.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers add WR Brandon Reilly, waive CB Alexander Myres|url=https://steelerswire.usatoday.com/2019/07/31/steelers-add-wr-brandon-reilly-waive-cb-alexander-myres/|work=Steelers Wire|publisher=USA Today|date=July 31, 2019}}</ref> On September 3, 2019, Myres was resigned to the Steelers' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alexander Myres back with Steelers on practice squad after missing camp with illness |url=https://triblive.com/sports/alexander-myres-back-with-steelers-on-practice-squad-after-missing-camp-with-illness/ |website=Tribe Live|date=26 September 2019 }}</ref> Myres signed a futures contract with the team on December 31, 2019, and was subsequently signed to the active roster on February 5, 2020 with appearances on all upcoming Steelers special teams formations.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alexander Myres|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/players/playerpage/3116872/alexander-myres|work=CBS Sports}}</ref>

On August 25, 2020, Myres was placed on injury reserve after tearing his groin muscle at practice.<ref>{{cite web |title=Steelers' Alexander Myres tears groin, on injury reserve. |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/steelers-alexander-myres-groin-injury/ |website=CBS Sports News}}</ref> August 30, 2020, Myres was waived by the Steelers to make room on the depth chart.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers make roster move|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-make-roster-move-at-wr|author=Varley, Teresa|website=Steelers.com|date=August 30, 2020}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===

Myres was notably recognized for being stiff-armed by Derrick Henry during his lone Lions appearance.<ref>{{cite news |title=Lions announce roster moves |url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-announce-roster-moves-vaitai-hand-skipper |website=DetroitLions.com |date=December 19, 2020 |access-date=February 3, 2021}}</ref> He was placed on the practice squad/injured list on December 29 after agitating his previous groin muscle tear at practice.<ref>{{cite news |author=Schlitt, Erik |title=Lions sign CB Josh Hawkins to practice squad, place CB Alex Myers on Practice Squad I.R. |url=https://lionswire.usatoday.com/2020/12/29/lions-sign-cb-josh-hawkins-to-practice-squad-place-cb-alex-myers-on-practice-squad-i-r/ |website=USAToday.com |date=December 29, 2020 |access-date=February 10, 2021}}</ref>

On November 20, 2022, Myres was selected by the [[Houston Roughnecks (2020)|Houston Roughnecks]] in the 5th round of the [[XFL (2020)|XFL]] draft.<ref>{{cite web |title=XFL Draft Recap 2022: Houston Roughnecks Day One Selections |url=https://xflnewshub.com/xfl-news/xfl-draft-recap-2022-houston-roughnecks-day-one-selections/ |publisher=XFL.com}}</ref> He was placed on the reserve list by the team on March 7, 2023, and activated on April 8.<ref name="XFL">{{cite web |title=XFL Transactions |url=https://www.xfl.com/xfl-transactions |website=XFL.com |access-date=March 14, 2023 |archive-date=March 16, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200316152142/https://www.xfl.com/xfl-transactions |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was released on June 22, 2023.<ref name="XFL"/>

'''Solomon Alijah Lewis Vera-Tucker''' (born June 17, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]] for the [[New England Patriots]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]], where he was awarded the [[Morris Trophy]] in 2020 and was a two-time [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference football teams|All-Pac-12]] selection. Vera-Tucker was selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the first round of the [[2021 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Vera-Tucker grew up in [[Oakland, California]] and attended [[Bishop O'Dowd High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hopkins |first=Justin |date=August 6, 2016 |title=Vera-Tucker Commits to USC |url=https://247sports.com/college/oregon/Article/4-Star-OL-Alijah-Vera-Tucker-Commits-to-USC-over-Washington-and-Others-46623753/ |access-date=September 24, 2020 |website=[[247Sports]]}}</ref> He played offensive tackle and defensive end on the football team and was named an Under Armour All-American as a senior.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 28, 2016 |title=Under Armour All-American Alijah Vera-Tucker goes from audience to honoree |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/alijah-vera-tucker-goes-from-audience-to-under-armour-all-american |website=[[USA Today]] |accessdate=September 24, 2020}}</ref> Vera-Tucker was rated a four-star recruit and committed to play [[college football]] at USC over offers from [[Washington Huskies football|Washington]], [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon]], [[Arizona Wildcats football|Arizona]], [[Arizona State Sun Devils football|Arizona State]], [[California Golden Bears football|California]], [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA]] and [[Washington State Cougars football|Washington State]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Polacek |first=Scott |date=August 5, 2016 |title=Alijah Vera-Tucker to USC: Trojans Land 4-Star OT Prospect |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2633884-alijah-vera-tucker-to-usc-trojans-land-4-star-ot-prospect |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |accessdate=September 24, 2020}}</ref>

==College career==
Vera-Tucker [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his true freshman season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaufman |first=Joey |date=November 12, 2018 |title=Redshirt freshman Alijah Vera-Tucker earning role as 'sixth man' |url=https://www.ocregister.com/redshirt-freshman-alijah-vera-tucker-earning-role-as-sixth-man-on-uscs-offensive-line |website=[[Orange County Register]] |accessdate=September 24, 2020}}</ref> Vera-Tucker played in all 12 of the Trojans games as a reserve guard and on special teams during his redshirt freshman season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eure |first=Keely |date=August 22, 2018 |title=OL Alijah Vera-Tucker has become USC's "sixth man" |url=https://247sports.com/college/usc/Article/Alijah-Vera-Tucker-USC-Football-interview-120936482/ |access-date=September 24, 2020 |website=[[247Sports]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kartje |first=Ryan |date=August 1, 2019 |title=USC's talent could spark revival in critical year for Clay Helton |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/usc/story/2019-08-01/usc-clay-helton-football-preview |access-date=June 11, 2022 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref> He was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference football teams|All-Pac-12 Conference]] by the [[Associated Press]]. Vera-Tucker considered entering the [[2020 NFL draft]], but opted to return to USC for his redshirt junior season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kartje |first=Ryan |date=January 18, 2020 |title=USC left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker to return |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/usc/story/2020-01-18/usc-alijah-vera-tucker-returns |access-date=June 11, 2022 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]]}}</ref> Following the announcement that Pac-12 would postpone the 2020 season due to the COVID-19 pandemic, Vera-Tucker announced that he would opt out of the season in order to focus on preparing for the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 10, 2020 |title=USC OL Alijah Vera-Tucker opts out to prepare for NFL draft |url=https://apnews.com/article/nfl-draft-football-drew-richmond-jay-tufele-southern-california-trojans-football-f5f7301e51b938a32722ad38941fd149 |website=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=September 24, 2020}}</ref> Vera-Tucker reversed his decision to opt out after the Pac-12 announced that they would resume fall football.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bonagura |first=Kyle |date=October 6, 2020 |title=USC offensive lineman Alijah Vera-Tucker opts back in to 2020 season |url=https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/30057233/usc-offensive-lineman-alijah-vera-tucker-opts-back-2020-season |access-date=October 8, 2020 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>
