===New York Jets===
Vera-Tucker was selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the first round (14th overall) of the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lange |first=Randy |date=April 29, 2021 |title=Jets Trade Up to No. 14 Overall, Pick Southern Cal OL Alijah Vera-Tucker |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/alijah-vera-tucker-nfl-draft-offensive-line-usc |access-date=May 7, 2021 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> He signed his four-year rookie contract with the Jets on July 20, 2021, worth $15.88 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Levine |first=Ben |date=July 20, 2021 |title=Jets Sign First-Round OL Alijah Vera-Tucker |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2021/07/jets-sign-first-round-ol-alijah-vera-tucker |access-date=June 11, 2022 |website=Pro Football Rumors |language=en-US}}</ref> He was named the Jets starting left guard, and started 16 games there, and was named to the [[PFWA All-Rookie Team]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2021 NFL All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2021.htm |access-date=2024-07-27 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Vera-Tucker was named the Jets starting right guard in 2022 after the team signed left guard [[Laken Tomlinson]]. He started at left tackle in Week 4 after an injury to [[George Fant (American football)|George Fant]], then moved to right tackle in Week 5 after an injury to [[Max Mitchell]], and started the next three games. He suffered a torn [[triceps]] in Week 7 and was placed on injured reserve on October 25, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Ethan |date=October 25, 2022 |title=Jets Place RB Breece Hall and OL Alijah Vera-Tucker on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-breece-hall-and-alijah-vera-tucker-injured-reserve-sign-zonovan-knight |access-date=May 19, 2023 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref>

Vera-Tucker returned as the Jets starting right guard in 2023. He moved to right tackle in Week 3 due to injuries. He suffered an Achilles injury in Week 5 and was placed on injured reserve on October 11, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Greenberg |first=Ethan |date=October 11, 2023 |title=Jets Sign WR Irvin Charles to Active Roster, Place Alijah Vera-Tucker on IR |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-wr-irvin-charles-to-roster-place-alijah-vera-tucker-injured-reserve |access-date=2024-08-28 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref>

On April 30, 2024, the Jets picked up the fifth-year option on Vera-Tucker's contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pullano |first=John |date=April 30, 2024 |title=Jets Pick Up Fifth-Year Option on OL Alijah Vera-Tucker |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-fifth-year-option-alijah-vera-tucker |access-date=2024-08-28 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref>

Vera-Tucker suffered a torn triceps in practice before Week 1 and was placed on season-ending injured reserve on September 6, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets starting RG Vera-Tucker out for season with torn triceps|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/46154805/source-jets-vera-tucker-triceps-season-ending-surgery|author=Cimini, Rich|work=ESPN|date=September 4, 2025}}</ref>

===New England Patriots===
On March 12, 2026, Vera-Tucker signed a three-year, $42 million contract with the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=March 12, 2026 |title=Patriots Announce Free Agent Signings |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-announce-free-agent-signings |work=[[New England Patriots]]}}</ref>

'''Alim McNeill''' (born May 11, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive tackle]] for the [[Detroit Lions]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[NC State Wolfpack football|NC State Wolfpack]], and was selected by the Lions in the third round of the [[2021 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
McNeill attended [[Jesse O. Sanderson High School]] in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stout |first=Jon |date=November 4, 2017 |title=Sanderson four-star DL Alim McNeill commits to NC State |url=https://www.highschoolot.com/sanderson-four-star-dl-alim-mcneill-commits-to-nc-state/17090322/ |access-date=February 6, 2023 |website=High School OT |language=en}}</ref> He played [[linebacker]] and [[running back]] in high school. McNeill committed to [[North Carolina State University]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pope IV |first=Jonas |date=November 4, 2017 |title=Four-star defensive line prospect Alim McNeill commits to NC State |url=https://www.heraldsun.com/sports/college/acc/nc-state/article182761771.html |access-date=February 5, 2023 |website=The Herald-Sun}}</ref> He also played baseball in high school.

==College career==
McNeill played at NC State from 2018 to 2020. During his career, he had 77 tackles, 10 sacks, one interception and one touchdown. As a junior, he was named an [[All-American]] by ''[[The Athletic]]'' and [[Pro Football Focus]] as well as earning All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] honors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=David |date=December 21, 2020 |title=Alim McNeil named All-American by Pro Football Focus |url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/2020/12/21/alim-mcneil-named-all-american-pro-football-focus/3990400001/ |access-date=February 5, 2023 |website=The Fayetteville Observer}}</ref> After that season, he entered the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pope IV |first=Jonas |date=December 5, 2020 |title=Alim McNeill, NC State nose tackle, headed to the NFL. Here's how he became a star. |url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/nc-state/article247577545.html |access-date=February 5, 2023 |website=The News & Observer}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Thompson |first=David |date=December 5, 2020 |title=NC State's Alim McNeil to forgo senior season, turn pro |url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/2020/12/05/nc-states-alim-mcneil-forgo-senior-season-turn-pro/3838675001/ |access-date=February 5, 2023 |website=The Fayetteville Observer}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gibson |first=Todd |date=December 14, 2020 |title=Known for wreaking havoc, NC State's Alim McNeill ready to tackle the NFL |url=https://www.cbs17.com/sports/nc-state/known-for-wreaking-havoc-nc-states-alim-mcneill-ready-to-tackle-the-nfl/ |access-date=February 6, 2023 |website=CBS17.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

McNeill was drafted 72nd overall by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the third round of the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Monarrez |first1=Carlos |last2=Alter |first2=Marlowe |date=April 30, 2021 |title=Detroit Lions pick DT Alim McNeill from North Carolina State in Round 3 of 2021 NFL draft |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2021/04/30/alim-mcneill-detroit-lions-nfl-draft-2021-round-3/4896497001/ |access-date=April 30, 2021 |newspaper=Detroit Free Press}}</ref> He signed his four-year rookie contract on May 13, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Links |first=Zachary |date=May 13, 2021 |title=NFL Draft Pick Signings: 5/13/21 |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2021/05/nfl-draft-pick-signings-51321 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |website=Pro Football Rumors |language=en-US}}</ref>

McNeill entered the 2023 season as the Lions starting defensive tackle. In Week 8, he recorded two sacks, his first career multi-sack game, and a pass deflection in a 26–14 win over the [[Las Vegas Raiders]]. He suffered a knee injury in Week 13 and was placed on [[injured reserve]] on December 5, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Risdon |first=Jeff |date=December 5, 2023 |title=Lions place DT Alim McNeill on I.R. in series of roster moves |url=https://lionswire.usatoday.com/2023/12/05/lions-roster-moves-alim-mcneill-injury-update-alualu-farniok-vildor/ |access-date=April 20, 2024 |website=Lions Wire |publisher=USA Today}}</ref> He was activated on January 6, 2024.<ref name="p596">{{Cite web |last=Reisman |first=Jeremy |date=2024-01-06 |title=Lions activate C.J. Gardner-Johnson, Alim McNeill; add 2 from practice squad |url=https://www.prideofdetroit.com/2024/1/6/24028006/detroit-lions-activate-cj-gardner-johnson-alim-mcneill-add-2-practice-squadders |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=Pride Of Detroit|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref>

On October 15, 2024, McNeill signed a four-year, $97 million contract extension with the Lions.<ref>{{cite web|title=Lions, DT Alim McNeill agree to terms on four-year, $97M extension|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/lions-dt-alim-mcneil-agree-to-terms-on-four-year-97m-extension|author=Gordon, Grant|website=NFL.com|date=October 15, 2024}}</ref> In Week 6's 47–9 victory over the [[Dallas Cowboys]], McNeill recorded two sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Detroit Lions at Dallas Cowboys - October 13th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202410130dal.htm |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In Week 15, McNeill tore his [[anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] in the 48–42 loss to the [[Buffalo Bills]], ending his season. Prior to the injury, McNeill recorded 25 tackles, 3.5 sacks, seven tackles for loss, and seven quarterback hits.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=December 16, 2024 |title=Alim McNeill out for season with torn ACL, Carlton Davis suffers fractured jaw |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/alim-mcneill-out-for-season-with-torn-acl-carlton-davis-suffers-fractured-jaw |access-date=2025-03-30 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref>

After spending the first six weeks of the season on the [[physically unable to perform|PUP list]], McNeill was activated for his season debut on October 20, 2025.<ref>{{cite web | last=Alper | first=Josh | title=Lions activate DT Alim McNeill | website=NBC Sports | date=2025-10-20 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/lions-activate-dt-alim-mcneill | access-date=2026-03-10}}</ref>

'''Alfred Haywood''' (born August 6, 1948) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] for one season in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Denver Broncos]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Bethune–Cookman Wildcats football|Bethune–Cookman Wildcats]]. He also played professionally for two seasons in the [[World Football League]] (WFL) as a member of the [[Jacksonville Sharks]] and [[Jacksonville Express]].

==Early life and education==
Born in [[Jacksonville, Florida]], on August 6, 1948, Haywood attended high school at [[Matthew Gilbert High School|Matthew W. Gilbert]], becoming one of three Gilbert attendees to play professionally.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/schools/high_schools.cgi?id=93bce274|title=Matthew W. Gilbert (Jacksonville, FL) Alumni Pro Stats|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> A two-sport star in baseball and football, he was offered professional baseball contracts from the [[Boston Braves (baseball)|Boston Braves]] and [[St. Louis Cardinals]] upon graduating high school.<ref name="auto1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/82758095/the-orlando-sentinel/|newspaper=[[The Orlando Sentinel]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=March 30, 1971|title=Haywood Rejects Football To Cast Lot With Baseball}} {{Open access}}</ref> He opted to attend college, going to [[Bethune–Cookman University]], serving as running back and kicker for [[Bethune–Cookman Wildcats football|their football team]] while playing catcher and slugger for [[Bethune–Cookman Wildcats baseball|their baseball team]].<ref name="auto1"/> He recorded 2,232 rushing yards and 1,411 receiving yards as the team's starting running back, and set a school record 52-yard field goal in 1970.<ref name="auto1"/> He earned All-Conference honors in three consecutive years.<ref name="auto1"/> He was described as "one of the best running backs in Bethune-Cookman College football history."<ref name="auto1"/> In baseball, he had a .588 batting average, including 5 runs batted in and a home run.<ref name="auto1"/>

==Professional career==
After going unselected in the [[1971 NFL draft]], Haywood was given nine offers to play in the [[National Football League]] (NFL), the largest totaling over $125,000.<ref name="auto1"/> He turned down the offers to pursue a career in professional baseball,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/82758035/the-miami-news/|newspaper=[[The Miami News]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=March 23, 1971|title=He Loves Baseball}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/82757961/the-miami-herald/|newspaper=[[The Miami Herald]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=March 23, 1971|title=Bethune Ace Turns Back On Football}} {{Open access}}</ref> saying "baseball was always my first love, even in high school. This was a very hard decision, because football is very much a part of me but baseball is in my heart."<ref name="auto1"/> However, he was not signed in baseball and shortly afterwards accepted an offer by the [[Miami Dolphins]] to play football. He was released during training camp.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/82757855/fort-worth-star-telegram/|newspaper=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=July 16, 1971|title=Untitled}} {{Open access}}</ref>

In 1974, after being out of football for two seasons, Haywood was signed to play for the [[Jacksonville Sharks]] of the newly formed [[World Football League]] (WFL). With the Sharks, he appeared in three games as a halfback, recording 20 rushes for 111 yards and 35 receiving yards on 7 receptions.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/playerh/hayw00200.html|website=Pro Football Archives|title=Alfred Haywood Stats}}</ref> He scored two touchdowns and also recorded one 1-point conversion.

When the Sharks folded in 1975, he joined the [[Jacksonville Express]]. He was their starting running back/fullback, appearing in 11 games. In a game against the [[San Antonio Wings]], Haywood scored a game-winning 15-yard touchdown in overtime to win, 26–19.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/82757738/the-news-and-observer/|newspaper=[[The News and Observer]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 24, 1975|title=Bell Startles Memphis '11'}} {{Open access}}</ref> In a game vs. the [[Shreveport Steamer]], he recorded over 120 yards to help his team win, 22–15.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/82755732/the-shreveport-journal/|newspaper=[[The Shreveport Journal]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=September 8, 1975|title=All Steamer Needs Is More Points|author=Woodson, Rick}} {{Open access}}</ref> He finished the season with 131 rushes for 687 yards and 4 scores. As a receiver he scored two touchdowns on 12 receptions for 131 yards, with a long of 37.<ref name="auto"/>

When the remainder of the [[1975 World Football League season]] was canceled, Haywood was acquired by the [[Denver Broncos]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/82755695/the-pensacola-news/|newspaper=[[The Pensacola News]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=November 12, 1975|title=Broncos Sign Alfred Haywood}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/82757750/the-monroe-news-star/|newspaper=[[The Monroe News-Star]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=November 12, 1975|title=Denver Acquires Alfred Haywood}} {{Open access}}</ref> The signing was announced on November 11. To make room on the roster, the Broncos released rookie linebacker [[Mike Lemon]]. Though scheduled to appear in their game against the [[San Diego Chargers]], Haywood would not appear in a game until December 14, in a 25–10 win over the [[Philadelphia Eagles]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HaywAl20/gamelog/|title=Al Haywood Career Game Log|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He would play in one other game, a 13–14 loss against the [[Miami Dolphins]] the next week. He recorded no statistics in his two games. In August 1976, he was released.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/82758775/casper-star-tribune/|newspaper=[[Casper Star-Tribune]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 21, 1976|title=Ramsey to start}} {{Open access}}</ref> A year later he was signed by the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL), but retired in June.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/82758886/edmonton-journal/|newspaper=[[Edmonton Journal]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=June 13, 1977|title=Argos give Eben a choice}} {{Open access}}</ref>

'''Alexander Wright''' (born September 5, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]] for the [[Cleveland Browns]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[UAB Blazers football|UAB Blazers]].

==Early life==
Wright grew up in [[Elba, Alabama]] and attended Elba High School.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 2, 2021 |title=Pro Football Focus names Elba native Alex Wright C-USA Defensive Player of the Year |url=https://www.elba-clipper.com/sports/pro-football-focus-names-elba-native-alex-wright-c-usa-defensive-player-of-the-year/article_06a29378-5391-11ec-b875-0b3f4b149578.html |access-date=February 16, 2022 |website=Elba Clipper}}</ref> He was named second-team All-State as a senior after recording 63 tackles, 17 tackles for loss, and 6 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stone |first=Nealand |date=January 3, 2019 |title=Four Elba Tigers named "All-State" in football |url=https://www.elba-clipper.com/sports/four-elba-tigers-named-all-state-in-football/article_13e84e2a-0f96-11e9-8fad-8b14c5a6a470.html |access-date=February 16, 2022 |website=Elba Clipper}}</ref> Wright committed to play [[college football]] at UAB over offers from Wake Forest, Duke, Tulane, Virginia, and Louisville.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mundee |first=David |date=December 19, 2018 |title=Elba's Wright signs with UAB; Eufaula's Hudgins with Jax State |url=https://dothaneagle.com/sports/high_school/elbas-wright-signs-with-uab-eufaulas-hudgins-with-jax-state/article_4f4fc892-03f9-11e9-9b9a-331a3268bcea.html |access-date=February 16, 2022 |website=[[Dothan Eagle]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Wright was named to the [[Conference USA]] All-Freshman team after recording 28 tackles, 8.5 tackles for loss, and 4.5 sacks with one forced fumble and two fumble recoveries.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dudley |first=Evan |date=December 20, 2019 |title='He's just gotta let it go': Alex Wright a force for UAB in freshman season |url=https://www.al.com/uab/2019/12/hes-just-gotta-let-it-go-alex-wright-a-force-for-uab-in-freshman-season.html |access-date=February 16, 2022 |website=[[AL.com]]}}</ref> As a sophomore, he had 17 tackles with three tackles for loss and one sack.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brugler |first=Dane |date=October 28, 2021 |title=NFL Draft Watch: My favorite under-the-radar prospects for April |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2917028/2021/10/28/nfl-draft-watch-my-favorite-under-the-radar-prospects-for-april/ |access-date=February 16, 2022 |website=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref> Wright was named second-team All-Conference USA after finishing his junior season with 46 tackles, 7.5 tackles for loss, seven sacks, and two forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Browning |first=Tyler |date=February 15, 2022 |title=UAB's Alex Wright could be part of solution to replenishing Cowboys edge department |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/uab-alex-wright-could-part-184703773.html |access-date=February 11, 2023 |website=Yahoo! Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> Following the end of the season, Wright declared that he would forgo his senior season and enter the 2022 NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dudley |first=Evan |date=December 26, 2021 |title=UAB's Alex Wright declares for NFL draft |url=https://www.al.com/uab/2021/12/uabs-alex-wright-declares-for-nfl-draft.html |access-date=February 16, 2022 |website=[[AL.com]]}}</ref>

'''Alfred Collins''' (born October 8, 2001)<ref name=birthday /> is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive lineman]] for the [[San Francisco 49ers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]] and was selected by the 49ers in the second round of the [[2025 NFL draft]].

== Early life ==
Collins grew up in [[Bastrop, Texas]] and attended [[Cedar Creek High School (Texas)|Cedar Creek High School]], where he lettered in football, basketball and track & field. In his high school career, Collins made 253 total tackles (180 solo and 73 assisted), 74.0 tackles for loss and 18.0 sacks. Collins would also make five pass breakups and five fumble recoveries.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/tx/cedar-creek/cedar-creek-eagles/athletes/alfred-collins/football/stats/?careerid=oda8m9nd9j0td|title=Alfred Collins' High School Football Stats|website=MaxPreps.com|date=October 22, 2022|access-date=April 10, 2024}}</ref> He played in the 2020 [[All-American Bowl (high school football)|All-American Bowl]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/college-football/news/alfred-collins-honored-as-a-2020-all-american|title=Alfred Collins Honored as a 2020 All-American|website=[[NBC Sports]]|first=Gus|last=Ramos|date=December 3, 2019|access-date=April 10, 2024}}</ref> Collins was a five-star rated recruit and committed to play college football at the [[Texas Longhorns football|University of Texas at Austin]] over offers from Alabama, Baylor, Oklahoma and Texas A&M.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/player/alfred-collins-46047351/high-school-201035|title=Alfred Collins, Cedar Creek, Strong-Side Defensive End|website=247sports.com|date=June 4, 2020|access-date=April 10, 2024}}</ref>

== College career ==
During Collins' true freshman season in 2020, he played in all 10 games and started one of them. He finished the season with 18 recorded tackles (11 solo and seven assisted), two tackles for loss, 1.5 sacks and two pass breakups.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alfred-collins-1/gamelog/2020/|title=Alfred Collins 2020 Gamelog|website=[[Sports Reference]]|access-date=April 10, 2024}}</ref> During the 2021 season, he played in all 12 games and started four of them, finishing the season with 25 registered tackles (15 solo and 10 assisted), five tackles for loss, two sacks, one forced fumble and four quarterback hurries.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alfred-collins-1/gamelog/2021/|title=Alfred Collins 2021 Gamelog|website=[[Sports Reference]]|access-date=April 10, 2024}}</ref> During the 2022 season, he played in 12 games and started one of them, finishing the season with 17 total tackles (seven solo and 10 assisted), three tackles for loss and one sack.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alfred-collins-1/gamelog/2022/|title=Alfred Collins 2022 Gamelog|website=[[Sports Reference]]|access-date=April 10, 2024}}</ref> During the 2023 season, he played in all 14 games and started six of them, finishing the season with 22 total tackles (12 solo and 10 assisted), two tackles for loss and two pass breakups.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alfred-collins-1/gamelog/2023/|title=Alfred Collins 2023 Gamelog|website=[[Sports Reference]]|access-date=April 10, 2024}}</ref> He was also named to the preseason watch list for the [[Senior Bowl|Reese's Senior Bowl]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.on3.com/teams/texas-longhorns/news/six-longhorns-invited-to-play-in-75th-reeses-senior-bowl/|title=Six Longhorns invited to play in 75th Reese's Senior Bowl|website=On3.com|first=Steve|last=Habel|date=November 17, 2023|access-date=April 10, 2024}}</ref>

On January 5, 2024, Collins announced that he would return to the Longhorns for the 2024 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/clemson/Article/texas-longhorns-football-alfred-collins-return-for-fifth-year-224526461/|title=Texas DL Alfred Collins confirms return to the Longhorns for the 2024 season|website=247sports.com|first=Chip|last=Brown|date=January 5, 2024|access-date=April 10, 2024}}</ref>
